title: AI: Add user access controls at course and activity level
description:
Currently, courses have limited means to control access to AI if it is switched on for the site - they can perform some capability overrides but this is complicated, cumbersome to access and not granular enough. In this issue, we will be implementing settings at the course and activity level, which enable more granular control in a user friendly interface (from within the existing settings pages teachers are already familiar with).
h3. User stories
 # As a teacher, I want the ability to turn AI tooling on or off at the course settings level, so it is easy to control access to that tooling in my course, and easy to find the setting.
 # As a teacher, I want the ability to define which AI actions are available within each activity in my course (or to turn it off completely per activity), to give me granular control over which of my activities have certain AI actions available.

h3. Requirements

Please see below for a link to the Figma protoype, which demonstrates how the following requirements should be implemented in the UI.
 # The course settings page will have a new "AI tools" section, which will contain a setting to turn AI on or off for that course.
 # Each activity's settings page will have a new "AI tools" section. If AI is turned on in course settings, the activity section will contain a setting to turn AI tools on/off for that activity, and if turned on for the activity, each AI action type will be listed and also be able to be turned on/off for that specific activity.
 # The course setting is the main switch for the course's AI availability - if it is on then activities can have AI turned on or off as above. If the course setting is off, then the activities cannot have AI turned on, it will still have an "AI tools" section, but the contents will be a message indicating AI must first be turned on in the course settings, instead of the actual settings.
 # Existing access measures are still in place. That means:
 ## If AI is not enabled on a site, it cannot be turned on at the course/activity level, and those areas should not display any AI settings. Note: Any values should be retained, so that if it is turned off and on again, previous settings are restored to the courses/activities.
 ## Existing capabilities should be honoured - for example if a student does not have the capability to use AI but a teacher does, then even if an AI action is enabled for an activity, only the teacher should have access to it (and the student should not see it at all).
 # All settings should be on by default (course, activity, all actions in activity) for new and existing sites. This retains existing functionality by default, since other requirements mean this only really makes AI available if it is turned on at the site level.
 # When the course level setting has AI switched off, we must retain all activity level settings (though they will have no effect), so that if AI tools are re-enabled on the course later, the existing configurations are still set and do not need to be configured from scratch on each activity.

The *[Figma prototype|https://www.figma.com/proto/EDxlKuUtAKkoAWXiiuPG85/AI-permissions-Prototype?page-id=0%3A1&node-id=1-262&p=f&viewport=472%2C534%2C0.05&t=Wf5R2r4Qc95jpllP-1&scaling=min-zoom&content-scaling=fixed&starting-point-node-id=1%3A262]* for this work demonstrates the above requirements and initial language strings required for the various states. The prototype flow is as follows:
 # Initial state: AI is enabled on the site but turned off in the course.
 # Visit activity in the course, expanding the AI tools section of settings advises you that AI must be turned on in the course to access the activity level settings.
 # Navigate to the course settings, and turn AI tools on for the course.
 # Return to the activity's settings, where the AI tools settings are now available, AI is turned on, and all AI actions are turned on for that activity.

h3. Out of scope
 # Any level of granularity not specified above.
 # Any new pages. All UI changes/additions here are within existing settings pages.
 # Bulk actions - this will be added as a follow up, and will make it possible to configure activities with the same AI settings simultaneously (for example, you could tick all quizzes and assignments and turn AI off, but turn it on with specific actions for other activities).

title: AI drawer should trap the keyboard focus within when it is open
description:
When the AI drawer is open, and the user tabs through its contents, the focus will move outside the drawer. 

On larger window sizes, this is okay. However, when the page is zoomed or viewed on smaller devices, this means that when the focus moves out of the open AI drawer, users may not be able to see which element has the focus when the open AI drawer obscures the element in focus. This scenario can cause us to fail the [WCAG 2.2 Level AA Success Criterion 2.4.11 Focus not obscured (minimum)|https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/focus-not-obscured-minimum.html].

One solution to this problem is to keep the focus within the AI drawer when it is open, so that it moves only within that area. 

Some things to keep in mind:
* By locking the focus on the AI drawer when it is open, we should designate the AI drawer with a dialog role and follow the [Dialog (Modal) Pattern|https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/] from the ARIA Authoring Practices Guide.
* Pressing the Escape key within the AI drawer should close it.
* Clicking on the AI action that opens the AI drawer should move the focus to the AI drawer.
* Assign an accessible name for the AI drawer. E.g. via {{aria-labelledby}} or {{aria-label}}.

title: Improve messaging experience for users who do not have permission to reply
description:
It is possible for a user to receive a message that they do not have permission to reply to, for example a teacher/admin may have the capability to message a student who does not have the capability to send messages. There is already handling in the backend to prevent the student in this example from sending a message, but there is no indication in the UI until they try to send a message:

!sending_rejected_error.png|width=200,height=183!

This is not a great experience because (a) the message is not very user friendly (using IDs etc), and (b) the timing of the message means the student would have to first write an entire message and hit send to see it, which is a frustrating experience that costs them unnecessary time.

The purpose of this issue is to make it more obvious in the UI _before_ the user tries to send a message. I would propose these requirements:

# Update the error message string so that it is more user friendly. We can probably make it more generic, for example "You do not have permission to send messages in this conversation".
# Persistently display the language string at the bottom of conversations the user cannot reply in, using the same elements currently displaying the error after they try to send the message. This should preemptively make it obvious to the user that they will not be able to reply to the message.
# If possible, disable the messaging textarea and/or send button, so it is really obvious to the user that they cannot send a message.
# We must retain the existing backend error functionality in addition to the above, particularly for security reasons, so that if someone trying to bypass the UI (eg sending directly via web service) that still receives an error response and the message is not sent.

I believe that the messaging textarea is common across all conversations, and it is possible that the user may be able to message some users and not others, so we will need to investigate whether that situation is possible (eg contacts vs non contacts), and if so, if it is possible to check whether the user is allowed to send in a conversation when that conversation is loaded, and if they don't have the access, disable the relevant form elements (and if they are allowed, make sure we re-enable the the elements so they can send messages in those cases). It also means we should not clear the text area when we disable or enable it, because the text carries between conversations and we don't want them to lose what they've written somewhere else if they flick between conversations.

title: Make ajax call for videojs cacheable
description:
When a student loads a video they first load an ajax web service which is then stored in , this is a redacted copy as curl:

curl 'https://www.example.com/lib/ajax/service.php?sesskey=k0BFVBG2LG&info=media_videojs_get_language' \
 
  -H 'x-requested-with: XMLHttpRequest' \
  --data-raw '[{"index":0,"methodname":"media_videojs_get_language","args":{"lang":"en"}}]'

This is sent with cookies and sesskey, and its a http post, but this is an unauthenticated ajax endpoint and the response is essentially unchanging static data. This should be highly cacheable.

So it should be sent as a http GET, with no sesskey, and the response should have cache expires headers so it can be cached at the cdn layer.

title: Add support for Symfony/Console for CLI Commands
description:
h2. Summary

Moodle's existing CLI support is based on a custom framework which has evolved over time and requires a significant amount of boilerplate to create and maintain commands.

This issue proposes adding support for the Symfony Console component as a modern framework for new core CLI commands. Symfony Console provides structured command definitions, argument and option handling, automatic help generation, improved output formatting, testing support, and a more consistent developer experience for creating command-line tools.

h2. Initial Scope

The initial implementation will:

* Add the Symfony Console dependency.
* Introduce a new {{bin/moodle}} entry point.
* Provide the infrastructure required to discover, register, and execute Symfony Console commands.
* Support command discovery using Moodle's existing namespace and class conventions.
* Provide standard global runtime options such as {{--showsql}} and {{--showdebugging}}.
* Include developer documentation describing how new commands are created, registered, and executed.

Symfony Console commands introduced by this issue may assume a configured Moodle installation and bootstrap Moodle through {{config.php}}.

h2. Existing CLI Scripts

Existing CLI scripts remain fully supported.

This issue does not seek to replace or remove the existing CLI framework. Existing scripts in {{admin/cli}} should continue to function as they do today.

Where equivalent Symfony Console commands are introduced, they should exist alongside the existing CLI scripts rather than replacing them.

h2. Proof of Concept

The proof of concept should demonstrate both the framework and a realistic command implementation.

This may include:

* Existing functionality exposed through Symfony Console commands (for example, cron-related commands).
* A modernised implementation of functionality currently provided by {{admin/cli/uninstall_plugins.php}}.

Rather than performing a direct one-to-one port of {{uninstall_plugins.php}}, the Symfony Console implementation should demonstrate a more focused command structure.

Examples may include:

{noformat}php bin/moodle plugins:list
php bin/moodle plugins:list --contrib
php bin/moodle plugins:list --missing

php bin/moodle plugins:uninstall mod_assign mod_forum
php bin/moodle plugins:uninstall mod_assign mod_forum --execute

php bin/moodle plugins:purge-missing
php bin/moodle plugins:purge-missing --execute
{noformat}

The existing {{admin/cli/uninstall_plugins.php}} script will remain available and unchanged.

h2. Out of Scope

The following are explicitly out of scope for the first iteration:

* Removal of existing CLI scripts.
* Migration of all existing CLI functionality.
* Plugin-provided Symfony Console commands.
* Installation and pre-installation commands that must operate without a configured Moodle site.
* Replacement of Moodle's existing CLI framework.

h2. Success Criteria

This issue will be considered complete when:

* Symfony Console is available in Moodle through Composer.
* The {{bin/moodle}} entry point can discover and execute Symfony Console commands.
* Commands can be registered using Moodle's standard namespace conventions.
* Proof-of-concept commands have been implemented.
* Developer documentation has been written.

title: Remove ltiinstance dependency from LTI Basic Outcomes service
description:
As with launches and other services, we need to remove any dependency on the 'lti' table (mod_lti's activity instance table), and use resource link dependency instead. This decouples the code from mod_lti.

For the Basic Outcomes (BO) service, we have the following areas to consider. BO was written before the service plugins, so has a single endpoint just for its own use (public/ltix/service.php). There is a service plugin too, but it only exists to shim basic outcomes support into LTI1p3 launches. Both are mentioned below.

*public/ltix/service/basicoutcomes:*

* This is the main BO service directory
* There are no references to lti instances that I've seen in here since this mostly exists to 

*public/ltix/service.php:*
This endpoint is the BasicOutcomes endpoint, and should not be confused with public/ltix/services.php (note the services is plural). By extension, this includes the \core_ltix\helper, which contains the implementation get_service_endpoint() and \core_ltix\local\ltiservice\service_helper which contains various implementations used by get_service_endpoint().

* In helper::get_service_endpoint():
** Instead of getting an lti record in this code ([https://github.com/snake/moodle/blob/ccc0ad6026803314fb58ab1a08c28b6709599f0b/public/ltix/classes/helper.php#L4156)|https://github.com/snake/moodle/blob/ccc0ad6026803314fb58ab1a08c28b6709599f0b/public/ltix/classes/helper.php#L4156)|smart-link]  we need to fetch a link where link.id = $parsed->instanceid.
* Rewrite service_helper::accepts_grades to operate on an resource_link object, not ltiinstance.
** This is used in get_service_endpoint().
** The existing mod_lti calling code (a deprecated method) will need to be updated to fetch the relevant link before calling the core_ltix method.
** The logic for the case where $ltitype->toolproxy is empty (i.e. non-lti2p0 cases), would be something like:
* {noformat}$acceptsgrades = $link->get('gradable') && ($toolconfig->lti_acceptgrades == constants::LTI_SETTING_ALWAYS || ($toolconfig->lti_acceptgrades == constants::LTI_SETTING_DELEGATE));{noformat}
** The logic for LTI2p0 remains the same.
* Rewrite service_helper::verify_sourcedid() to operate on a resource_link, not an ltiinstance. All that's needed from the link is it's servicesalt, e.g. $link->get('servicesalt')  
** this is also used in get_service_endpoint()
** the existing mod_lti calling code (a deprecated method) will need to be updated to fetch the relevant link before calling the core_ltix method.
* Rewrite service_helper::update_grade() to operate on a resource_link, not an ltiinstance.
** Getting a reference to the activity instance is the challenging bit, since we've deliberately tried to decouple that and use resource_link as an abstraction layer, but we have what we need. It's a combination of:
*** Check: is the link gradable? If so, continue.
*** Check: is the link tied to a course module context? If so, continue (this assumes that, for now, only course module context placements of links can be gradable. could change in future).
*** Now, using the module context, get the mod instance + course
** The grade_update proceeds as is currently is, using $ltiinstance, because we've now fetched that.
** update the get_record('lti_submission'); call to query based on resource_link id, not instance id.
** continue to update the update/insert calls for lti_submission the same way, using resource_link id instead of ltiinstance->id.
** the existing mod_lti calling code (a deprecated method) will need to be updated to fetch the relevant link before calling the core_ltix method.
* Rewrite service_helper::read_grade() to operate on a resource_link, not an ltiinstance.
** Just like in update_grade(), we need to fetch the mod instance and course from the resource_link.
** Then, fetching grades remains unchanged.
** the existing mod_lti calling code (a deprecated method) will need to be updated to fetch the relevant link before calling the core_ltix method.
* Rewrite service_helper::delete_grade() to operate on a resource_link, not an ltiinstance.
** Just like in update_grade(), we need to fetch the mod instance and course from the resource_link.
** Then, deleting grades remains unchanged.  
** the existing mod_lti calling code (a deprecated method) will need to be updated to fetch the relevant link before calling the core_ltix method.

*lti_submission table definition:*

* lib/db/install.xml: rename ltiid to ltiresourcelinkid and update the comment.
* No upgrade fix is needed. All resource links created as part of site upgrade have been given the exact same ids as the mod_lti instance tables to which they belong, meaning we can already query lti_submission by link id.

*Regression testing (This only tests replaceResultRequest/grade update though):*

* Use Moodle-to-Moodle LTI using LTI1p1.
* Publish an assignment or something in the tool course
* Set up a link to the published assignment in the platform site course
* Launch into the assignment link as a student
* Launch into the assignment link as an admin and grade the student
* run the 1p1 grade sync task in the tool site:

{noformat}php admin/cli/scheduled_task.php --execute="enrol_lti\\task\\sync_grades"{noformat}

* We can likely also test using the Saltire test tool, which might allow us to test readResultRequest and deleteResultRequest too.

description:
Following the introduction of the LTI Placement concept, several existing settings from the "Tool settings" section of the LTI external tool creation page have been relocated to the Placement configuration settings, while some have become redundant. This issue aims to remove those outdated and redundant settings from the tool creation form. ”Allows you to customise the icon displayed for this LTI tool. Instead of the default LTI icon, you may specify an icon that better represents the tool’s purpose or functionality.”

title: Marking workflows: Phase 1 - Support multiple markers and grade calculations
description:
Phase 1 of the Double Marking project.

*AIMED RELEASE:* 5.1 / 5.2

*MAIN FUNCTIONALITY:* ”Double Marking with Marker allocation - joint feedback, separate grade, manual feedback agreement”

----

Phase 1 of the Double Marking project introduces the ability for multiple markers to be allocated to a student’s assignment submission, where they can set individual marks to be calculated into a final grade, via various methods.



Currently, the terms “grade” and “mark” are used somewhat interchangeably in Moodle. This project introduces a clear distinction between the two.

*grade* - is still as it was, the overall final value for an assignment

*mark* - is a separate value set by a “marker”. Think of it as a “provisional grade”.



There can be between 1 and 5 markers allocated to a student submission.

Where you have more than 1 marker, the following options exist for calculation of final grade:

* manual - No automatic calculation. Someone must manually review the marks and choose the final grade.
* first - In this case, the first mark added will be chosen as the final grade
* max - In this case the highest mark added will be chosen as the final grade
* average - In this case an average of the marks added will be chosen. This option has further options to choose how the average is calculated: round up, round down, natural rounding, no rounding



An example workflow for an assignment with 2 allocated markers:

* Assignment created by a teacher, with settings (markingallocation=yes, markingworkflow=yes, markercount=2, multimarkingmethod=max)
* A teacher/manager with “manageallocations” capability can set which teachers are allocated to which students, either on a case-by-case basis using Quick Grading page, Advanced Grader window, or the Bulk Allocate Markers page. E.g. Teacher 1 and Teacher 2 allocated.
* Teacher 1 uses the Quick Grading page and sets a mark of “45” for Student 1
* Teacher 2 uses the Advanced Grader page and sets a mark of “99” for Student 1
* Automatic calculation is run using method “max” and “99” is chosen and set for Student 1’s grade



As well as marks, the workflow state can also be set by the allocated markers and calculated automatically.

The logic for this is:

* If ALL markers have set their mark state to “Marking Complete” then the overall grade workflow state is set to “Marking Complete”.
* If ANY marker has set their mark to anything higher than “Not Marked”, e.g. “In Marking” or “Marking Complete”, then the overall grade workflow is set to “In marking”
* ELSE it is set to “Not Marked”



As well as individual assignments, this also supports Group/Team submissions, in the following way:

* Markers can either be allocated to every student in the group (probably most common) or they can only be assigned to some members of the group
* Marks and workflow states can be set on specific users via the Quick Grading page, like grades can be currently
* Marks and workflow states can be applied to the entire group via the Advanced Marker page, like grades can be currently. However, in this case, they are only applied if the marker is allocated to the student in the group.



Feedback can be left by all markers, however it is currently just in 1 text area and not split into different sections per marker. That is for a later phase of the project.

The new functionality works for Simple grading, such as point or scale, but not for rubrics or marking guides. They will be investigated in a later phase of the project.



*Notes*

* If a user wants to use the functionality how it used to be (currently is, prior to this being integrated), they can set a marker count of 1. They will then still be able to set individual marks and individual workflows, but they don’t have to use them, they can just set the grade and the overall workflow state and ignore the marking option.

title: Marking workflows: Phase 2 - Improved feedback handling (including separate marker feedback for multiple markers)

Once we have answers to the above we can better plan and estimate the delivery issue.

description:
{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Policy: PHP & Moodle supported versions*

Since Moodle 3.5 ([MDL-59159|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-59159]), these rules apply to decide the Minimum PHP and Moodle versions supported:

# An LTS will always require the previous LTS (or later) for upgrading.
# The maximum PHP version supported for a branch will be the maximum one achieved throughout the life of the branch. Usually with .0 releases, but it may happen later (we added support for php70 with 3.0.1 or support for php73 with 3.6.4, for example).
# The minimum PHP version supported for a branch will be *the lower of*:
#* The [minimum version supported in any way by php|http://php.net/supported-versions.php] that is under support for at least 12 more months when the new Moodle version gets released (so we provide slow, progressive increments).
#* The maximum PHP version supported by the previous LTS branch (so we guarantee jumping between LTS is possible without upgrading PHP at the same time).
{panel}

We need to decide ASAP about all the PHP/DB/Moodle version requirements and put all of them into the environmental tests (adding them to all supported branches).

All the still open linked issues have also been cloned here from the 5.1 sister issue (MDL-85362).

Usual discussions:

* PHP minimum version/[supported versions|https://secure.php.net/supported-versions.php].
* Database versions.
* Linked issues.

title: Create API allowing placements to query a link's expected launch container
description:
Placements don’t determine the launch container for links. Tools control this via their config (see ”Default launch container” in the configuration form).

When placing a link, a placement should have access to the relevant information about the expected launch mode so it can make decisions about how to present the link (whether that may be an <a> tag, or embedded HTML, or otherwise). 

For example, in the mod_lti case, it is essential to know what the whether the tool is configured to launch links in a new window. This knowledge allows mod_lti to create the link with a relevant onclick handler in the lti_get_coursemodule_info() callback, meaning a user clicking the activity name will instantly be taken to a new window launch of the tool. If the tool isn’t configured for new window launches, then we don’t want this onclick handler. 

I think it’ll be useful to ask core_ltix for the launch container for a _link_, rather than for a _tool_, however (at least in terms of how we express this in an API method name). Calling something like foo::get_launch_container__for_link_() allows greater flexibility in future if/when we decide to let links control their desired launch mode/presentation mode (per the value returned during deep linking). Right now, we can certainly just delegate to the tool’s configuration within such a method.

So, what we’d like to do:

# Create the above API in a sensible place
## This should currently just lookup the tool’s default launch container
# Tests for the above, which really just consists of creating a link for a mock placement of a tool, then checking that we get back the value currently configured on the tool.

title: Users are getting "Invalid request" when sending their badges to Canvas Credentials
description:
Friday, 13 June 2025, Instructure sent an email to announce the phasing out of free issuer capabilities in Canvas Credentials by December 31st, 2025:

* June 30th, 2025  – The ability to create a new free issuer will no longer be possible.
* Dec 31st, 2025 – Free issuing capabilities end. Free issuers will no longer be able to issue badges or export data.  The issuer will turn into a backpack essentially. They will not be deleted.

 

So currently, in some scenarios, users are getting an “Invalid request” error when sending their badges to Canvas Credentials backpack using OBv2.0.



*Steps to reproduce*

# Login as admin.
# Go to Site administration > Badges > Manage backpacks.
# Edit the existing “[https://badgr.io|https://badgr.io]”, select the “Include authentication details with backpack”, and set Badge issuer email and password (using a valid Canvas Credentials user).
# Create a badge and award it to a user.
# Login as the user and connect to the [https://badgr.io|https://badgr.io] backpack using a different user. You’ll need to confirm the account (by accessing the email client and verifying it).
# Go to the user profile page.
# Open the badge and click the “Send to backpack” button.



*Current behaviour*

The “Invalid request” error is displayed because the issuer can’t be created in the Issuer Canvas Credentials account defined in step #3.

!Screenshot from 2025-07-28 16-50-13.png|width=1285,height=642,alt="Screenshot from 2025-07-28 16-50-13.png"!

!Screenshot from 2025-07-28 16-54-21.png|width=637,height=190,alt="Screenshot from 2025-07-28 16-54-21.png"!



*Expected behaviour*

The badge is sent to Canvas Credentials (even if the issuer can’t be created in the Issuer Canvas Credentials account).

Apart from that, instead of displaying “Invalid request”, the message should be replaced to give more information to the user in other situations (because the server is returning the reasons why the badge can’t be added).

In [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-85949|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-85949|smart-link], the XD team prepared a proposal for the error message on the badge recipient’s side. This is a generic message for any error that occurs when a user tries to add a badge to a backpack from the badge page:

{quote}*Can’t add badge to backpack*
Your backpack provider is sending this message: ‘[Error from provider]’.

You can try downloading the badge and adding it manually to your backpack, or try again later.{quote}



Swagger UI for Canvas Credentials OBv2.0: [https://api.badgr.io/swagger-ui/index.html|https://api.badgr.io/swagger-ui/index.html]

title: Ad-hoc task mod_qbank\task\transfer_question_categories causes performance issues on large sites
description:
Due to some (unknown) bug that causes massive question duplication, we have millions of question copies. There’s one question category with 1.070.303 questions.

The ad-hoc task {{mod_qbank\task\transfer_question_categories}} goes through all top question categories and calls {{qbank_managecategories\helper::question_remove_stale_questions_from_category}} for every sub-category. This loads ALL questions into RAM, which are either old-style random questions (qtype = random) or any questions that were deleted while they were in use by a quiz (status = hidden), but whose usages have since been removed.

{code:sql}SELECT q.id
FROM mdl_question q
  JOIN mdl_question_versions qv ON qv.questionid = q.id
  JOIN mdl_question_bank_entries qbe ON qbe.id = qv.questionbankentryid
WHERE qbe.questioncategoryid = :categoryid
  AND (q.qtype = 'random' OR qv.status = 'hidden');{code}

Then, {{question_delete_question()}} is called on every question. This creates another couple of dozen SELECT and DELETE statements for every question. We can roughly delete 500 questions per minute. This takes way too long to comb through 15 million questions.

Running the following query

{code:sql}SELECT qbe.questioncategoryid, count(qbe.questioncategoryid) as numberofquestions
FROM mdl_question q
         JOIN mdl_question_versions qv ON qv.questionid = q.id
         JOIN mdl_question_bank_entries qbe ON qbe.id = qv.questionbankentryid
WHERE (q.qtype = 'random' OR qv.status = 'hidden')
GROUP BY qbe.questioncategoryid
HAVING numberofquestions > 10000
ORDER BY numberofquestions DESC;{code}

gives me 68 question categories with between 1.071.300 and 10.257 questions each. That’s 15.064.429 questions combined from a total of 16.962.840 questions.



We need to make this more efficient.

title: Move report entity initialisation boilerplate into base class
description:
The base report entity “initialise()” method is [currently abstract|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/reportbuilder/classes/local/entities/base.php#L94-L105], to be implemented by all entity classes themselves

What has happened is that each implementation of this abstract method is essentially identical/duplicated between all entity classes:

* [https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/badges/classes/reportbuilder/local/entities/badge.php#L69-L89|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/badges/classes/reportbuilder/local/entities/badge.php#L69-L89|smart-link]
* [https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/message/classes/reportbuilder/local/entities/conversation.php#L56-L76|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/message/classes/reportbuilder/local/entities/conversation.php#L56-L76|smart-link]
* [https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/tag/classes/reportbuilder/local/entities/instance.php#L69-L90|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/tag/classes/reportbuilder/local/entities/instance.php#L69-L90|smart-link]
* … etc (there are approximately 37 copies of this method)

The only variation is for those entities that include custom/profile fields:

* [https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/reportbuilder/classes/local/entities/course.php#L75-L105|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/reportbuilder/classes/local/entities/course.php#L75-L105|smart-link]
* [https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/reportbuilder/classes/local/entities/user.php#L75-L105|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/0ec57fc3f2826cebdb36335bfab9f2703378d99d/public/reportbuilder/classes/local/entities/user.php#L75-L105|smart-link]
* … etc (there are 5 copies of this method)

In this issue:

# Make “initialise()” a concrete method of the base class
# Make it call new methods “get_available_[columns|filters|conditions]()”
# Replace custom implementation of the above in all entities

The methods from 2. being added to the base class are new, and intended to replace “get_all_[columns|filters]()” methods that have become the de-facto standard of all entity classes (although they were never part of the API). We aren’t re-using these method names in the base class, because in some entity instances these methods receive parameters (in Workplace)

The changes here should be entirely backwards compatible. Third party code will continue working as before, because they already implement the previously abstract “initialise()” method themselves

All hail glorious [~accountid:5b68b573e147c03be566836c] for the idea

|givenname|firstname|

However, the claims passed by Microsoft are underscored versions of these, they should be:

|external field|internal|
|family_name|lastname|
|given_name|firstname|

The result is, if a new Oauth2 service is enabled and Oauth2 users are allowed to create an account on first login, they will not be able to proceed as their first and lastname fields will be blank.

I’ve tested this on the Moodle 5.0 sandbox ,[https://sandbox.moodledemo.net/|https://sandbox.moodledemo.net/|smart-link]  and confirmed accounts are missing first and last name with the default configuration. Changing the field mappings as mentioned resolves the issue:

title: Update security.txt for 5.2 release and related minors
description:
In [MDL-69877] a new security.txt file, following the information @ [security.txt|https://securitytxt.org/] was introduced.

The security.txt file located in _public/security.txt (or security.txt pre 5.1)_ must be updated regularly, shortly before it expires (defined by the {{Expires}} element within the file).

+*The updates should be made to main, as well as all other security supported Moodle versions that contain security.txt.*+ This means all supported versions have an identical security.txt file (including the same expiry).

This task must only land in the minor release versions that are scheduled for release alongside the relevant major release  (for example if 5.2 is the major release, then 5.1.3 will be one of the minors receiving the update). Therefore, the ideal window for landing this issue is +2-6 weeks prior to release+.

As a minimum, this will involve updating the {{Expires}} value, which needs to be set to *[expected subsequent major release date]* *+ 3 WEEKS*. This provides a small buffer in case the major release is delayed. If any of other details in the security.txt need to be amended, they should also be completed at the same time. We should also check the RFC in case of any changes (see the [Github repo|https://github.com/securitytxt/security-txt] to check if any versions have been released since the previous LMS release).

----

Detailed information (to be modified for each clone of this issue):

* *Branches affected:* main (5.2), 5.1, 5.0, 4.5
* *Expiry (5.3 release + 3 weeks):* 5 October 2026 + 3 weeks =  26 October 2026
* *Commit message:* MDL-XXXXXX core: Update security.txt expiry
* *Other changes:* _... add any further changes required here_

Exact formatted expiry date to use: *2026-10-26T01:00:00.000Z*

How the date format was calculated (in line with the [latest spec|https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-foudil-securitytxt-12#section-3.5.5]):

{{date --date='26 October 2026 01:00' -u +"%FT%H:%M:%S.000Z"}}

----

(This issue is part of the release process, 2 weeks before release, and will be cloned as part of it.)

title: Add Moodle 5.1.0 upgrade line to all the upgrade.php scripts
description:
To have it properly detected for the future, it would be great to add to all the upgrade.php scripts some lines like these:

{code:php}// Automatically generated Moodle v5.1.0 release upgrade line.
// Put any upgrade step following this.{code}

exactly before the "{{return true;}}" present in all the scripts.

Normally, it's ok to do that both in the stable (501_STABLE) and the {{main}} branches, so they will allow quickly find where 5.1.0 started and act once we decide future requirements.

But, *when under parallel development, this only can be done in the stable (501_STABLE) branch* as the {{main}} branch already has diverged and can have own upgrade steps not corresponding to the version just released, but to the future version being developed in parallel.

The change can be performed globally with:

{code:java}#!/bin/bash
export rel="5.1.0" && find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | \
grep '/db/' | \
xargs grep -L "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
xargs perl -p -i -e 's@( *)(return true;)@\1// Automatically generated Moodle v$ENV{rel} release upgrade line.\n\1// Put any upgrade step following this.\n\n\1\2@s'{code}

*Command to detect* all the upgrade.php files not having those lines:

{code:java}find . -name upgrade.php | xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | grep '/db/' | xargs grep -L 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.0.0 release upgrade'{code}

*Commands to detect* that we have not added the lines to incorrect files:

{code:java}grep -lr 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.1.0 release upgrade' * | grep -v '/db/'
grep -lr 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.1.0 release upgrade' * | xargs grep -L 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade'{code}

*Command to detect* if the lines have been added after a post-release upgrade step. If there are upgrade steps found, verify that all of them were already there the day of the release and have not been introduced later (you can look for differences between the release v5.0.0 and the current {{main}} branch to verify that)

{code:java}export rel="5.1.0" && export ver="202510" &&
find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -B25 "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
grep "upgrade_.*_savepoint.*${ver}"{code}

*Important note to integrators*: The sooner this issue is integrated after release, the fewer chances to get the lines put in an incorrect place (that's what the last "command to detect" above tries to avoid. We need to ensure that the lines are *exactly* at the release point (or we may end up deleting upgrade steps incorrectly in the future). So, immediate integration after release (within the on-sync period and ideally before any new upgrade step is added), it the best achievement.

Ciao 🙂

title: Decide Moodle 5.3 requirements and push them to environment.xml (Due date: 29-05-2026)

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Final 5.3 agreed environment requirements*

* PHP 8.3 (ruled).
* Moodle 4.4.0 is required for upgrades (ruled).
* PostgreSQL 17 (*changed*)
* MySQL 8.4
* Amazon Aurora MySQL 8.0

*Policy: PHP & Moodle supported versions*

Since Moodle 3.5 ([MDL-59159|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-59159]), these rules apply to decide the Minimum PHP and Moodle versions supported:

# An LTS will always require the previous LTS (or later) for upgrading.
# The maximum PHP version supported for a branch will be the maximum one achieved throughout the life of the branch. Usually with .0 releases, but it may happen later (we added support for php70 with 3.0.1 or support for php73 with 3.6.4, for example).
# The minimum PHP version supported for a branch will be *the lower of*:
#* The [minimum version supported in any way by php|http://php.net/supported-versions.php] that is under support for at least 12 more months when the new Moodle version gets released (so we provide slow, progressive increments).
#* The maximum PHP version supported by the previous LTS branch (so we guarantee jumping between LTS is possible without upgrading PHP at the same time).
{panel}

We need to decide ASAP about all the PHP/DB/Moodle version requirements and put all of them into the environmental tests (adding them to all supported branches).

All the still open linked issues have also been cloned here from the 5.1 sister issue (MDL-85362).

title: Activity completion override ignores passing grade
description:
When a teacher overrides a student’s activity completion via the activity completion report it always gets stored as {{COMPLETION_COMPLETE}} in the {{course_modules_completion}} DB table regardless of whether the student has a passing grade. If the student has a passing grade and the teacher completes an activity for them it should get stored as {{COMPLETION_COMPLETE_PASS}} instead.

This bug prevents students from accessing activity B which requires completion of activity A with a passing grade - even though a teacher has both marked activity A as completed for them and given them a passing grade in activity A (regardless in which order the teacher has done this).

title: Hooks Manager MUST NOT use MUC
description:
The Hook Manager currently uses the MUC system to cache hooks, overrides, and the override hash.

These things are all very deterministic, and there may be cases where we need to use hooks before MUC or the database are configured.

This is such a low level API that it should not have any dependence upon MUC.

It can exist in {{localcache}} or {{cache}} instead.

Note: If it exists in {{localcache}} then the detections for override cache being different on different nodes will not be picked up (which is a problem).

title: UX copy improvement for the Cancel button on /login/ when the user is already authenticated

{quote}“You are already logged in as XXXXXX, you need to log out before logging in as different user.”{quote}

…and two buttons: *“Cancel”* and *“Log out”*.

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a student, or Admin.
# Manually go to {{https://YOUR-MOODLE/login/}}.
# Observe the dialog.

h2. Current result

* Informational message is shown.
* Buttons: *“Cancel”* and *“Log out”*.
* *“Cancel”* does not clearly convey that it simply closes the dialog and returns to the site.

h2. Expected result

* Keep the informational message.
* Replace *“Cancel”* with a contextual label, e.g. *“Back to site”* / *“Return to Moodle”*.
* Alternatively, clarify in the body text what each action does.

title: CORS policy error from YouTube repository when importing
description:
Discovered when reviewing for [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-85930|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-85930|smart-link].

When you are using the YouTube repository, and importing media, there is a step in the JS logic where it attempts to determine what type of file it is (video vs. audio). There is a fetch to YouTube headers which is disallowed resulting {{in:}}

{{Access to fetch at 'https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DubiRbeDpnM#What%20is%20Moodle%20LMS?%20Latest%20release%20video'  from origin 'http://localhost' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource.}}

To replicate:

# Set up the YouTube repository (need an API key)
# Create a course and Page resource
# Click the ‘Multimedia’ icon on the TinyMCE toolbar
# Click ‘Browse repositories’
# Choose the YouTube repository in the file picker.
# Search for a term (e.g. Moodle)
# Press ‘Search’
# Open your browser’s console and observe the error message.

The solution may be as simple as removing the check in {{loadMediaPreview()}}

{{this.mediaType ??= await checkMediaType(url);}}

This check is only used here and may have very limited application.

title: SCORM packages that open in a new window should inform users that they open in a new window
description:
Teachers can configure a SCORM package to display in the current window or in a new one.

title: Chrome 142 Local Network Access restrictions break LTI
description:
Hello!

Chrome 142 turned on restrictions about public servers accessing things on the local network: [https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access|https://developer.chrome.com/blog/local-network-access|smart-link] 

For use this broke the LTI for Turn It In, when Launch container = Embed. This shouldn’t be specific to Turn It In though, any embedded LTI that authenticates with a Moodle server with a private IP address will fail on Chrome 142 and later. The iframe loads these URLs:

# {{https://moodle-server/mod/lti/launch.php?id=4&triggerview=0}}
# {{https://lti.int.turnitin.com/oidc/login/xxx}}
# {{https://moodle-server/mod/lti/auth.php}} (fails with LocalNetworkAccessPermissionDenied)

Our {{moodle-server}} has split-horizon DNS, on campus users get a 10.x.x.x IP, Internet users get a public IP. [lti.int.turnitin.com|http://lti.int.turnitin.com] has public IPs.

I added “local-network-access *” in mod/lti/view.php where it builds the <iframe allow="">attribute. Now Chrome prompts for local network access permissions and then loads the LTI. Other LTIs that don’t redirect back don’t prompt for local network access.

It feels Chrome is wrong, but the sane fix is in Moodle.  And the only fix is in Moodle code. Or changing our network.

Thanks!

*Replication steps:*
Run a Moodle instance on localhost or a private IP. Add an LTI activity hosted on a public IP. The LTI has to authenticate back to the original Moodle. Chrome 142 will display an error instead of showing the LTI:

“The connection is blocked because it was initiated by a public page to connect to devices or servers on your private network. Reload this page to allow the connection.”

Reloading the page doesn’t work.

title: Subsections: Remove subsection pages
Subsections: Remove description from settings page
Subsections: Create a task to remove existing descriptions
description:
This issue tracks the implementation of improved, linear navigation for course content by *creating a task to remove the subsection descriptions from the database*.

h2. 💡 Research and discovery decisions

Based on research into the desired course linear navigation experience, the following architectural and UX decisions were made:

* *Subsection descriptions removed:* Support for subsection descriptions will be *discontinued*. The subsection settings page will be streamlined to contain only the *Name* and *Restrict access*. This will be implemented in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87279|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87279|smart-link] 
* *Strategy for handling existing descriptions*: To ensure data preservation during the upgrade, existing subsection descriptions will *not be removed* from the database.
** *Data preservation:* Existing subsection description data will be *retained* in the database upon system upgrade.
** *Migration tasks for admins:* The following maintenance tasks will be provided to administrators to handle the deprecated data:
**# *Remove descriptions:* A task to delete all existing subsection descriptions from the database permanently.
**# *Migrate to Text&Media:* A task to convert existing subsection descriptions into standard *Text&Media* resources within the course structure.
** *Task status:* These tasks will be *disabled by default* to allow administrators to choose their preferred method of data handling.

h2. ✅ Implementation tasks

This issue should implement the first task, to remove descriptions from the database permanently. Requirements:

# Create a scheduled task.
# Place the task within the subsection module.
# The task must perform a permanent database deletion of the specified description data.

*Note*: This cleanup task is *temporary*. It is scheduled for complete removal in Moodle 7.0, at which point the entire description functionality will be permanently deprecated and removed from the database: [MDL-87466|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87466]





➕ More information can be found in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Moppies/pages/3390144515/Remove+subsections+page|https://moodle.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/Moppies/pages/3390144515/Remove+subsections+page|smart-link]

title: Navigation footer: Adapt width to account for course index
description:
Currently, the sticky footer component renders across the *full width of the viewport*.

This behaviour conflicts with the intended layout as defined in the XD prototypes: when the *Course index* is visible and pinned, the sticky footer *overlaps* and covers the bottom portion of the index area:

!image-20251125-174129.png|width=671,alt="image-20251125-174129.png"!

This negatively impacts usability and design integrity by obscuring the future navigation controls.



h3. *Required action*

The sticky footer must be constrained (shrunk) so that it only occupies the horizontal space available *next to* the vertical drawers for the course index and the blocks:

!image-20251125-173931.png|width=671,alt="image-20251125-173931.png"!

h3. 

h3. *Acceptance criteria*

* When the Course index is visible, the sticky footer *does not overlap* any part of the index or the blocks. 
* When the Course index and the blocks are hidden, the sticky footer should expand to the whole page.
* The footer continues to function correctly (e.g., sticking to the bottom) regardless of screen width.

title: Navigation footer: Add a setting to enable/disable the linear course navigation for topics/weeks
description:
The goal is to provide course creators with explicit control over the visibility and functionality of the new *Linear course navigation* (Previous/Next) buttons within the sticky footer. This setting will allow teachers to disable the feature if it conflicts with their course design or preferred navigation method.

h3. 🎯 *Required action*

* Add a new course format setting for the Custom sections and the Weekly sections course formats that allows users to toggle the Linear course navigation on or off for courses. [Check the prototype|https://www.figma.com/design/0jNMdb7sBnlOuSfwrHp0Ph/2025-%C2%B7-Course-linear-navigation?node-id=2517-46621] for the names/descriptions of these settings:
** For existing courses, changing the course format *will not change the Enable linear navigation* setting. 
!image-20260430-112444.png|width=600,alt="image-20260430-112444.png"!
* Add a site-level default setting for Custom sections and another for Weekly sections to let admins define the default value for the course setting. It should be enabled by default. [Check the prototype|https://www.figma.com/design/0jNMdb7sBnlOuSfwrHp0Ph/2025-%C2%B7-Course-linear-navigation?node-id=2517-47950] for the names/descriptions of these settings:
!image-20260430-112540.png|width=600,alt="image-20260430-112540.png"!
* Implement a {{supplementary_sticky_footer}} component, ensuring it is rendered at the bottom of the viewport on *all activity view pages*. For this first version, the footer must contain a single, clearly identifiable button "Back to course". This button must link the user directly back to the main course page from which the activity was launched.

h3. (/) *Acceptance criteria*

* A new configuration setting is visible and functional within the settings page for both Custom sections and Weekly sections course formats.
* A new site-level setting for both Custom sections and Weekly course formats to let admins define the default value for the previous setting. The setting's default value is set to *ON* (enabled).
* When the setting is *enabled*, the linear navigation buttons are displayed in the sticky footer.
* When the setting is *disabled*, the linear navigation buttons are *not* displayed in the sticky footer.
* For existing courses, linear navigation will not be enabled when a site is upgraded.

title: Technical spike - TinyMCE RTL menu navigation keyboard behavior
description:
While investigating [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86812|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86812|smart-link], we discovered that TinyMCE's keyboard navigation in dropdown menus with submenus does not behave correctly in RTL (Right-to-Left) mode. In RTL languages, pressing the Left Arrow key should open submenus (moving right in RTL context), and Right Arrow should close them. Currently, the behavior remains in LTR mode regardless of the directionality configuration.

After peer review discussions, we determined this is an upstream TinyMCE issue rather than a Moodle-specific problem. The TinyMCE menu navigation logic uses hardcoded LTR arrow key handling and does not expose a supported API to override these keybindings for RTL mode.

An initial workaround was implemented using keyboard event interception to swap left/right arrow keyCodes in submenu contexts. However, this approach is fragile, depends on internal TinyMCE DOM structures, and would likely break on future TinyMCE upgrades while potentially interfering with built-in accessibility behavior.

The purpose of this technical spike is to:

# Report the issue to the TinyMCE team via GitHub (completed)
# Monitor and track the upstream response and any potential fixes

title: Automatically add report entity joins to all applicable elements
description:
Applicable elements = all column, conditions & filters of the entity

We currently have the following for every entity element:

{noformat}$ git grep '\->add_joins($this->get_joins())' | wc -l
380{noformat}

Example: [https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/8cb5d000a1fd45eebeea6e4bd2cda09621d2e6f7/cohort/classes/reportbuilder/local/entities/cohort.php#L114|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/8cb5d000a1fd45eebeea6e4bd2cda09621d2e6f7/cohort/classes/reportbuilder/local/entities/cohort.php#L114|smart-link]

Report builder should be cleverer than that, and explicitly add all entity joins to these elements by default, requiring only additional joins required by them to be added ([like this one|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/8cb5d000a1fd45eebeea6e4bd2cda09621d2e6f7/cohort/classes/reportbuilder/local/entities/cohort.php#L115]). This change is in a similar spirit to in our efforts to reduce the amount of boilerplate that goes into implementing the reportbuilder APIs (like [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87404|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87404|smart-link] et al.)

In this issue:

* Adding report elements to entities should automatically add all joins added to the entity when it’s added to a report
** Any joins subsequently added by a column _must_ come after the “default joins” added above
* Remove those 380 lines as now no-ops
* Add upgrade note detailing this change of behaviour

title: Behat named selector for interacting with Toast elements
description:
In Workplace we have _lots_ of Behat steps similar to the following:

{noformat}And I wait until ".toast-message" "css_element" does not exist
...
And I should see "Foo" in the ".toast-message" "css_element"

title: Handle file uploads with filenames exceeding 255 characters gracefully
description:
*Description:* When a user attempts to upload a file with a filename exceeding 255 characters, the operation fails due to the {{VARCHAR(255)}} constraint on the {{filename}} column in the {{mdl_files}} table.

Screenshot below per XMLDB in moodle sandbox

!Screenshot 2025-12-17 at 12.21.46 pm.png|width=671,alt="Screenshot 2025-12-17 at 12.21.46 pm.png"!

Currently, this results in a database write error rather than a user-friendly validation message. Furthermore, when testing with extremely long filenames (e.g., >500 characters), the resulting error message in the Boost theme renders incorrectly, causing text to overflow bounds and become illegible.

*Technical Context:* The {{mdl_files}} table schema restricts filenames to 255 characters.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

# Create a dummy file on your local machine with a filename longer than 255 characters (e.g., 300+ characters). If you hit a character limit on your local system, continue anyway.
# Log in to Moodle.
# Navigate to any activity that accepts file uploads (e.g., Assignment, File Resource, or Private Files).
# Attempt to upload the file via drag-and-drop or the file picker.
Where you’re prompted for the file name in the picker, make the text larger than 255 characters (I just typed garbled words and copy pasted)

*Actual Result:* The upload fails, triggering a database exception regarding the {{VARCHAR}} constraint. The user interface may display a generic error or, in cases of very long filenames, a broken UI element where the error text overflows the container (specifically observed in the Boost theme).


!image-20251217-015628.png|width=671,alt="image-20251217-015628.png"!

*Expected / Suggested Behavior:* The system should handle long filenames in one of the following ways:

# *Schema Update:* Increase the {{VARCHAR}} constraint in {{mdl_files}} to accommodate longer filenames.
# *Auto-Truncate:* Automatically shorten the filename to fit within the 255-character limit (preserving the file extension) and notify the user.
# *Theme fix:* If the {{VARCHAR}} constraint in {{mdl_files}} should not be changed, make corrections to theme so that the error message displays correctly. Truncating the file path in the error, or not displaying it at all if that makes things appear better.

title: Oauth2 linked login expired requests are never deleted
description:
When you set up Oauth2 authentication for users already created with other auth types, an email is sent to confirm the linked login, and if the users clicks on the link inside that email in a 30 minute period the linked login becomes established.

[https://docs.moodle.org/n/OAuth_2_authentication|https://docs.moodle.org/n/OAuth_2_authentication]

[https://docs.moodle.org/en/Linked_logins|https://docs.moodle.org/en/Linked_logins]

The issue happens when that 30 minute period expires and the user haven’t confirmed the linked login; in that case if the user tries to login via OAuth2 again Moodle throws an error message (_This account is pending email confirmation._) and therefore the user cannot start the process again and gets locked.

I’ve seen that this requests are stored in mdl_auth_oauth2_linked_login, so I’ve been able to clean up the expired tokens executing this query:

{noformat}delete from mdl_auth_oauth2_linked_login aall
 where(   aall.confirmtokenexpires<>0
      and to_timestamp(aall.confirmtokenexpires)< CURRENT_TIMESTAMP - INTERVAL '30' MINUTE
      );{noformat}

but I’d say:

* There should be a place inside Moodle to remove expired requests (both as a users and as an admin)

and/or

* There should be an scheduled task that removes all the expired requests

title: Authentication: New installs force login on by default
description:
Change the default setting for “Force users to log in” (Site admin → Security → Site security settings) from No/disabled to Yes/enabled, for new installs only. Existing installs / upgraded sites should keep their default settings even if not explicitly changed.

Currently for new installs, users are presented with a blank “home” page, with a very small login Call To Action. (image below).

!Screenshot 2025-12-23 at 08-12-04 Home Moodle Demo.png|width=800,alt="Screenshot 2025-12-23 at 08-12-04 Home Moodle Demo.png"!



This makes it confusing for first time users of new sites to understand what they need to do to login and use, or for admins login and configure the site. As the login CTA is small it is hard to see, and it also may not be immediately apparent that you are not logged in immediately after install.

By changing the “Force users to log in” to Yes/enabled, all users will be presented with a familiar login workflow. This will reduce confusion and help provide new users with a better first time experience.

!Screenshot 2025-12-23 at 08-12-32 Log in to the site Moodle Demo.png|width=500,alt="Screenshot 2025-12-23 at 08-12-32 Log in to the site Moodle Demo.png"!

title: Routing: Handle "Next" behaviour for final course activity
description:
The current ‘Next’ routing logic identifies the subsequent activity in the course sequence and redirects the user.

The goal of this issue is to update the navigation handler to detect when the user is on the final activity of the course and redirect the ‘Next’ action to the main course page.

h3. 🎯 Required action

* Implement logic to detect if the current activity is the *last item* in the course sequence. Check:
** If a subsequent activity exists, redirect to that activity.
** If no subsequent activity exists (i.e., the end of the course), redirect the user to the course’s main page.
* *Ignore* the logic that accounts for hidden activities or restricted content that might "end" the visible sequence for a specific user.

h3. (/) Acceptance criteria

* Applying ‘Next’ to the final activity of a course successfully redirects the user to the course page.
* The behaviour for non-final activities remains unchanged (redirecting to the next activity).

title: Routing: Handle "Previous" behaviour for first course activity
description:
The current ‘Previous’ routing logic identifies the preceding activity in the course sequence and redirects the user.

The goal of this issue is to update the navigation handler to detect when the user is on the first activity of the course and redirect the ‘Previous’ action to the main course page.

h3. 🎯 Required action

* Implement logic to detect if the current activity is the *first item* in the course sequence. Check:
** If a preceding activity exists, redirect to that activity.
** If no preceding activity exists (i.e., the start of the course), redirect the user to the course’s main page.
* *Ignores* the logic accounts for hidden activities or restricted content that might "end" the visible sequence for a specific user.

h3. (/) Acceptance criteria

* Applying ‘Previous’ to the first activity of a course successfully redirects the user to the course page.
* The behaviour for non-final activities remains unchanged (redirecting to the previous activity).

title: Routing: Integrate section pages into linear navigation sequence
description:
In the initial implementation, the ‘Next’ and ‘Previous’ routes skipped directly between activities, bypassing section landing pages (e.g., jumping from the last activity of Section 1 directly to the first activity of Section 2).

This issue involves updating the navigation logic to include *section pages* as valid destinations in the linear sequence. The goal is to ensure users encounter the section’s introductory content before moving into the activities within that section.

h3. 🎯 Required action

* Redefine the "linear" path to include: _Last activity of a section → Section page_ and _First activity of a section → Section page_.
** On the *last activity* of Section 1, the ‘Next’ route should now point to the *Section 2 landing page*.
** On the *first activity* of Section 2, the ‘Previous’ route should point back to the *Section 2 landing page*.

h3. (/) Acceptance criteria

* Section landing pages are displayed during sequential navigation.
* The ‘Next’ and ‘Previous’ routes correctly identify the immediate parent section or adjacent section pages based on the course hierarchy.
* Ensure that navigation remains continuous even if a section has no activities.

title: Routing: Handle behaviour for restricted activities (Next and Previous)
description:
The linear course navigation must correctly handle activities that are hidden or restricted based on access rules (e.g., date restrictions, grade requirements, or completion of prerequisites). We need to ensure that the ‘Next’ and ‘Previous’ routes lead students to the expected pages (the new restricted implementation in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87283|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87283|smart-link]).

h3. 🎯 Required action

* Ensure that restricted activities hidden from students (eye closed) are skipped in the linear sequence for students.
* Confirm that restricted activities displayed to students (eye open) are included in the linear sequence (and the new page implemented in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87283|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87283|smart-link] is displayed).
* The navigation sequence must update dynamically as a student unlocks new activities.

h3. (/) Acceptance criteria

* Students must not see a ‘Next’ or ‘Previous’ route pointing to an activity that is fully hidden from their view.
* If an activity is visible but restricted (locked in the course index), going to ‘Next’ must navigate to that activity to show the restriction requirements.
* *Restricted subsections* must be included in the navigation logic to ensure they behave consistently with restricted individual activities.
* Verify that teachers can still navigate through all activities (including hidden/restricted ones) to review the course flow.

title: Routing: Handle behaviour for restricted sections
description:
The linear course navigation must correctly handle *Sections* that are hidden or restricted based on access rules. We need to ensure that the 'Next' and 'Previous' routes lead students to the expected pages, specifically respecting the restricted section implementation (and the corresponding landing pages for restricted content).

h3. 🎯 Required action

* Ensure that sections marked as ‘Hidden’ from students (restricted with eye closed or hidden) are entirely skipped in the linear sequence, including all activities within them.
* Confirm that sections that are restricted but visible to students (eye open) are included in the linear sequence. 'Next' should lead to the section landing page where restriction requirements are displayed.
* The navigation sequence must update dynamically as a student unlocks a previously restricted section.

h3. (/) Acceptance criteria

* Students must not see a ‘Next’ or ‘Previous’ route pointing to a section (or its contents) that is fully hidden from their view.
* If a section is visible but restricted (locked), going to ‘Next’ from the previous activity must navigate the user to that section's landing page to show why it is locked.
* Verify that teachers/admins can still navigate through all sections (regardless of hide/restrict settings) to preview the full course flow.

title: Navigation footer: Implement a mechanism to add exceptions and implement them for the Assignment pages
description:
This issue tracks the implementation of an exception rule to suppress the sticky footer rendering for the Assignment activity in the following cases:

* Add submission
* Edit submission

h3. 🎯 *Required action*

* Implement a mechanism to conditionally disable the {{core_sticky_footer}} component rendering for specific views.
* Identify the {{mod_assign}} controller state where {{action=editsubmission}} or when the submission form is present in the output buffer.
* Ensure that the footer reappears immediately once the submission is saved or if the user returns to the assignment "View" (intro) page.

h3. (/) *Acceptance criteria*

* The sticky footer is *visible* on the Assignment intro page, where the instructions are displayed.
* The sticky footer is *hidden* automatically when a student clicks "Add submission" or "Edit submission".

title: TypeError when trying to use \core\route\require_login for courseless login checks
description:
I’m trying to implement a controller for a non-course-centric route, using the following attribute helper:

{noformat}...
requirelogin: new require_login(
    requirelogin: true,
    autologinguest: false,
)
...{noformat}

This is synonymous with the old require_login(null, false); login is required, but not for a course.

Currently, the above results in a TypeError because moodle_authentication_middleware calls $requirements->get_course_attribute_name(), which is typed to return a string (but actually is a nullable param underneath). If we’re not setting that param in the attribute declaration, then it’s null and results in that TyepError. Additionally, in the middleware, $courseorid is conditionally set, only if we’re able to get this courseattributename. 

I think we want to support null in the login helper -  i.e. make get_course_attribute_name() return null or string - and then support null as a valid value for $courseorid in the middleware, so we can then pass this along to require_login() there too. It seems this was the intention of this code, as there’s already calls to require_login there - hence reporting this as a bug for now.

title: Convert Entity Custom Field Category to Shared Category
description:

* After the conversion, a toast should be displayed with a confirmation message.
* If a shared custom field category with the same name already exists, the conversion should still proceed without errors.
* If any custom field within the category being converted has a short name that already exists in a shared custom field category, the conversion must be blocked. In this case, display a notice to the user explaining why the conversion cannot proceed.
