title: Marking workflows: Phase 3 - Add basic sample marking for multiple markers
description:
h1. *Multiple Marking – Phase 3 updated 2026 Jun*

This document is an [+updated version of previous signed off requirements+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1ko-PNO0BUlgYnFrZ8WU5RTC5JUAXhqCUSR1BKiJd7LY/edit?tab=t.0] by Monash team. The major updates are:

*Assignment level setting:*

* “Maximum total markers” → "Number of required markers" (This is covered in the [+meeting notes+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W_TsbgLLRpxgIXPLukzQlPBRQTER6-ANpfqF8R4JpyA/edit?tab=t.0])
* “Number of optional markers limit’ → "Number of optional markers" (This is covered in the [+meeting notes+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1W_TsbgLLRpxgIXPLukzQlPBRQTER6-ANpfqF8R4JpyA/edit?tab=t.0])

*Site level setting terminology update:*

* “Maximum total markers limit” → “Maximum required markers limit” (This is confirmed in the [+MDL tracker+|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87709] comments by Michael)
* “Maximum number of optional markers limit” → “Maximum optional markers limit” (This is confirmed in the [+MDL tracker+|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87709] comments by Michael)

h1. Summary and Background:

Multiple Marking Phase 3 delivers two key enhancements that build on the functionality introduced in Phase 1 and Phase 2. These enhancements aim to improve marking governance, usability, and operational efficiency.

*Part 1: Basic Sample Marking*

This component enhances and extends the existing multiple marking framework introduced in Phase 1.

Key improvements include:

* Introduction of site-level marker settings to provide stronger governance and configuration control.
* Support for more detailed and flexible marking configurations.
* Improved consistency in the user experience when marking students.

This enhancement ensures a more scalable and controlled multiple marking model, reducing configuration ambiguity and improving marking reliability across units.

*Part 2: Filter Assignment Submissions by Grade*

This component enhances the Advanced Filter functionality on the View All Submissions page.

Key improvements include:

* Additional filtering capabilities based on grade values.
* Ability to sort students by grade.

These enhancements make the multiple marking feature more practical and efficient for coordinators and markers, particularly in large cohorts where grade analysis and targeted review are critical.

h2. *Part 3a - Basic Sample Marking*

These requirements define the configuration and behaviour of multiple markers in assignments using sample marking. They cover site-level and assignment-level settings, constraints on marker numbers, rules for increasing or reducing markers, grade calculation and recalculation, marker reassignment, and related UI behaviour. The intent is to ensure consistency, protect existing marking data, and provide clear, predictable outcomes for all students.

h2. 1. Configuration

1.1 Update the naming in the *assignment setting*:

* Update field name ‘Marker’ to ‘Number of required markers’
* Add a new field: ‘Number of optional markers’

*Site-level configuration*

h2. 1.2 *Maximum* required markers limit

The system should allow the site administrator to configure the maximum required markers limit at the site level. This value should be used as the maximum selectable value in the ‘Number of required markers’ dropdown in the assignment settings. When creating or editing an assignment, users must only be able to select marker values up to the configured site maximum.

* Any changes to the site-level maximum must be reflected immediately for newly created assignment configuration interfaces. 
* Any reduction to the site-level maximum setting should not impact existing assignments. All existing assignments should retain their current required marker without any changes.

h2. 1.3 *Maximum* optional markers limit

The system should allow the site administrator to define the maximum optional markers limit at the site configuration level. This value should be used as the upper limit for the *‘*Number of optional markers*’* dropdown within assignment settings. When creating or editing an assignment, users must only be able to select marker values up to the configured site maximum.

* Any changes to the site-level maximum must be reflected immediately for newly created assignment configuration interfaces. 
* Any reduction to the site-level maximum setting should not impact existing assignments. All existing assignments should retain their current optional marker settings without any changes.

h2. 1.4 *Default* number of required markers

The system should allow a site administrator to configure the ‘default number of required markers’ at the site level. The default required markers value should be less than or equal to the configured ‘maximum required markers limit’ value. This default value should be pre-selected in the number of required markers selection dropdown in the assignment settings.

h2. 1.5 *Default* number of optional markers

The system should allow a site administrator to configure the ‘default number of optional markers’ at the site level. The default optional markers value must be less than or equal to the configured ‘maximum optional markers limit’ value. This default value should be displayed and pre-selected in the number of optional markers selection dropdown in the assignment settings.

*Site Level Validation*

1.6 When a site administrator adjusts ‘maximum required markers limit’ or ‘maximum optional markers limit’, existing assignments must retain the existing selection values. The existing marker selection, marks and grades should be retained. When the updated value is saved, it will apply and display to newly created assignments. 

*Assignment Setting and Validation*

1.7 [+Number of required markers (Required markers)+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TfY2F8YXv_P4Wz1Q-BryMhwDUbnSY2yzkC-QvOmpaG8/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.nbrpy7yj5ok1] define the number of required markers that can be assigned to a student. 

1.8 [+Number of optional markers (Optional markers)+|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1TfY2F8YXv_P4Wz1Q-BryMhwDUbnSY2yzkC-QvOmpaG8/edit?tab=t.0#bookmark=id.nbrpy7yj5ok1] defines the optional number of markers that can be assigned to a student. 

1.9 In the assignment settings, the number of required marker selection dropdowns must not allow a value of 0. The minimum selectable value must be greater than 0.

1.11 Number of required markers, Number of optional markers, increasing or decreasing required or optional markers applies to all students in the unit.

----

h2. 2. Marker Numbers and Grade Calculation

2.1 The system should calculate and display a grade (in the grade column) when:

* If required markers are allocated and no optional markers are enabled, all required markers have marked and marking workflow status is set to marking completed. 
* If one or more required markers have not entered a mark (marking status is not _marking completed_), the system must not calculate or display a grade.

*OR*

* If required markers + optional markers enabled, all required markers and all enabled optional markers have marked and marking workflow status is set to Marking completed.
* Optional markers that are not enabled (unchecked checkboxes) must be ignored for grade calculation.

2.2 When grade has been calculated. If an optional marker is enabled (e.g., checkbox ticked), existing markers mark and feedback should be retained, if the grade already exists display a pop up asking for a confirmation that grades will be cleared/reset to null/empty. When an optional marker has been assigned and marked, the system will calculate the grade.

2.3 In the assignment setting, changing the calculation method (e.g., from average to maximum) is allowed at any time, even post mark release, it requires user confirmation (e.g., popup: "This will update agreed grades for all students. Yes?"). If the user selects yes, It triggers grade recalculation for all affected students. If user select no, the calculation method remain unchanged

----

h2. 3. Increasing Marker Numbers

3.1 Increasing the required/optional markers should be applied to all students in the assignment. The system evaluates each student individually, and the configuration change applies to all the students within the assignment.

3.2 In assignment setting, increasing the required markers is allowed at any time. All the markers’ marks, feedback and grades are retained. When the required markers are increased, the number of optional markers must remain unchanged.

Example: Required marker is 2 and optional marker is 2, increasing required marker from 2 to 3

* When Marker 3 and 4 have not been assigned/marked, the system will increase the required marker to 3, optional markers will shift to marker 4 and marker 5.
* When Marker 3 and 4 have been assigned/marked, the system will increase the required marker to 3, marker 3 and 4 will shift to marker 4 and marker 5. Optional markers’ marks, feedback and grades are retained.

3.3 In assignment setting, increasing the optional markers is allowed at any time. All the markers’ marks, feedback and grades are retained. When the optional markers are increased, the number of required markers must remain unchanged.

Example: Required marker is 2 and optional marker is 2, increasing optional marker from 2 to 3

* When Marker 3 and 4 have not been assigned/marked, the system will increase the optional marker to 3, the newly added optional markers will be marker 5.
* When Marker 3 and 4 have been assigned/marked, the system will increase the optional marker to 3, the newly added optional markers will be marker 5. Marker 3 and 4s’ marks, feedback and grades are retained.

----

h2. 4. Reducing Marker Numbers

4.1 Reducing the required/optional number of markers, this should be applied to all students in the assignment. The system evaluates each student individually, and the configuration change applies to all the students within the assignment.

4.2 In assignment setting, reducing the required markers are allowed when:

* The marker being removed has not been assigned to the student.

Example: Required marker is 5 and optional marker is 0, 

* If Marker 5 has been not been assigned to any student, the total number of markers can be reduced to 4 (removing Marker 5). 
* If Marker 5 has been assigned to any student, the total number of markers cannot be reduced.

4.3 In assignment setting, reducing optional number of markers is allowed when:

* The marker being removed has not been assigned to or enabled for any student.

Example: If the required marker is 2 and the optional marker is 2, marker 4 has been enabled and allocated to one student, for other students marker 4 is not enabled, in the assignment setting the optional number of markers cannot be reduced.

Example: Required marker is 4 and optional marker is 1, reducing optional marker from 1 to 0

* When Marker 5 has not been assigned or enabled to any student, the number of optional markers can be reduced to 0. 
* When Marker 5 has been enabled but not assigned, the number of optional markers limit can not be reduced to 0. 
* When Marker 5 is assigned, the number of optional markers limit can not be reduced to 0.

----

h2. 5. Reassign Marker

5.1 Reassigning a marker is only permitted when the assigned marker’s marking status is ‘Not marked’. Once the marker has marked, or the marking status is anything other than ‘Not marked’, it cannot be reassigned to another marker.

----

h2. 6. UI Rules for total marker, minimum marker, optional marker slots

6.1 The required markers allocation slots show with no checkbox. (Refer to UI example 1)

6.2 The optional marker slots show an "Enabled" checkbox (unchecked by default). When checked, user can select markers. (Refer to UI example 1)

description:
For PHPUnit’s configuration to work with both:

* moodle in its current form; and
* moodle installed via Composer and in a sub-directory relative to the {{vendor}} directory

We need to make the phpunit.xml.dist and generated phpunit.xml point to testcases and coverage data within a sub-directory.

That looks like:

{noformat}.
├── moodle
│   └── public
│       ├── admin
│       │   └── tool
│       │       └── phpunit
│       │           └── cli
│       │               └── init.php
│       └── mod
│           └── forum
│               └── tests
│                   └── example_test.php
└── phpunit.xml{noformat}

For the new approach, vs:

{noformat}.
├── phpunit.xml
└── public
    ├── admin
    │   └── tool
    │       └── phpunit
    │           └── cli
    │               └── init.php
    └── mod
        └── forum
            └── tests
                └── example_test.php{noformat}

title: Integrate and optimise React build code into core
description:
We have done our discovery work on adding react into core. This issue is for reviewing the code on [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|smart-link] and make sure that it adheres to Moodle coding guidelines, makes improvements where possible, and does not cause any regressions
One of the completion criteria is ensuring that developer documentation is provide. 

When working through this issue, please consider:

* Identify code that is no longer needed
* Remove any experimental scaffolding
* Simplify any code that we put in to produce a working result
* Challenge if each part is needed
* Reduce complexity if possible

*Merge plan*

This issue introduces Esbuild as the build system for React code in Moodle. The primary architectural decision is the introduction of a dedicated {{js/react/}} directory, keeping React logic physically and logically separate from legacy AMD code.

*Dedicated Source Organisation*

React source files are located in {{js/react/src/}} rather than {{amd/src/}} because they are native ES modules and are not processed through Moodle’s AMD pipeline.

* *Location:* {{[plugin]/js/react/src/ }}(additional subdirectories may be defined beneath src/ as needed)
* This separation clearly distinguishes React-based code from AMD modules and prevents existing Grunt/Shifter tasks from attempting to process files they do not support.

*Output Format and Build Integration*

While the code lives in a new folder, *Esbuild* is configured to output the transpiled results in a way that our existing systems can still understand.

* *Multiple Entry Points:* Esbuild maps each file in {{js/react/src/}} to a corresponding output in {{js/react/build/}}.
* *Format Consistency:* We utilize Esbuild's flexibility to ensure the output remains compatible with Moodle's page requirements manager, even though it lives outside the traditional {{amd/}} folder.
* *Zero Config Discovery:* The build script automatically scans all {{js/react/}} directories across the entire Moodle tree. The discovery occurs at build time and does not affect runtime performance.

*Benefits of the js/react/ separation*

* *Gradual transition:* Features can transition from AMD / YUI to React without restructuring existing modules
* *Linting & Tooling:* We can apply stricter TypeScript and React-specific linting rules (MDL-87988) to the {{js/react/}} folder without triggering thousands of "legacy" errors in the old {{amd/}} code.

*Centralised Bundling:* By centralising React code here, Esbuild can more efficiently handle *Tree Shaking* and *Dynamic Imports*, ensuring that we don't duplicate the React runtime across different plugins.

title: Fix bug in lib/lti1p3 causing omitted line item properties to be sent as nulls during deep linking return
description:
This is one of two blockers to using the new certification tooling at build.1edtech to certify (or re-certify) our LTI Provider as LTI Advantage Complete. Right now, during a deep linking workflow, after content selection (and assuming “add to gradebook” IS checked), the cert. suite reports:

{noformat}"errors": [
    "'label' should be a string",
    "'tag' should be a string"
],{noformat}

Moodle doesn’t set label or tag on the lineitem when returning it as part of the content item, however. See the code responsible for that response here:
[https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/f747c15cbf1c1c963a9592a73b167b969ec33d75/public/enrol/lti/configure.php#L76|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/f747c15cbf1c1c963a9592a73b167b969ec33d75/public/enrol/lti/configure.php#L76|smart-link] 

What should happen is that, because we’ve omitted those fields (i.e. we’re not calling setLabel() or setTag()), the label and tag properties should be excluded from the contentitem’s lineitem. These fields are optional per the spec: [https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-dl/v2p0#lti-resource-link|https://www.imsglobal.org/spec/lti-dl/v2p0#lti-resource-link|smart-link]  

If these fields are omitted, the certification suite’s diagnosis window reports everything is green and passing.

I’ve reported this bug upstream([https://github.com/packbackbooks/lti-1-3-php-library/issues/169|https://github.com/packbackbooks/lti-1-3-php-library/issues/169|smart-link] ), but even when that lands and we upgrade our library, it won’t fix the issue in stables. We need to patch that locally if we want to use the new certification site for the re-certification of stable+sec versions - and we do, since it saves ~90 mins per Moodle version being certified + is more accurate, which is win-win for us.

title: Minor change in curl class breaks Microsoft O365 plugin
description:
We have identified that the change to the {{PUT}} method signature in the {{curl}} class — introduced in the following commit: [https://github.com/moodle/moodle/commit/161837e393b84ce43525eb88250689bc059b3f0a|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/commit/161837e393b84ce43525eb88250689bc059b3f0a|smart-link] has broken compatibility with the Microsoft O365 plugin. This caused a 500 error across all our platforms, preventing users from authenticating via OIDC : 


{noformat}PHP Fatal error:  Declaration of local_o365\httpclient::put($url, $params = [], $options = []): string|bool must be compatible with curl::put($url, $params = [], $options = [], $includeuserpwd = true) in /var/www/html/local/o365/classes/httpclient.php on line 160{noformat}

A straightforward merge request has been submitted to Microsoft: [https://github.com/microsoft/o365-moodle/pull/3019|https://github.com/microsoft/o365-moodle/pull/3019|smart-link] 

However, I am questioning whether it is standard practice for such a breaking change to occur within a minor update of version 5.0. Perhaps this is not an intended change, which is why I’m reporting it here.

title: New page surfaces and activity card states
description:
h3. Design rationale

Activity cards have no fill and no border, so they don't react to the pointer or the keyboard.

A section body can hold twenty activities. With no edge between them they read as one undifferentiated list, and you have to use the text to work out where one activity stops and the next begins. Giving each card a border makes the section scannable at a glance.

Hover fills the card white so you can see which one the pointer is on as you move down a long section. Focus goes back to grey with a blue ring instead, so keyboard position never gets confused with mouse position: two different questions, two different answers.

The subsection chevron is currently smaller than the section chevron. That implies subsections are a lesser kind of thing, which isn't true — they're a peer structure, and should look like one.

h3. What needs changing

*Activity card states*

||State||Fill||Border||
|Rest|{{$mds-bg-surface-subtle}} {{#f8f9fa}}|1px {{$mds-border-default}} {{#dee2e6}}|
|Hover|{{$mds-bg-surface-default}} {{#ffffff}}|unchanged|
|Focus|back to {{#f8f9fa}}|{{$mds-border-interactive-primary-default}} {{#0f6cbf}} + ring|
|Hover + focus|{{#ffffff}}|as focus|

* The fill at rest is the same grey as the body behind it, so the border is the card's only edge.
* Focus must not change the card's size — outline and shadow, not border width.
* Same behaviour inside a section and inside a subsection. A subsection renders _inside_ an activity card so exclude it or the whole subsection lights up. Only the edit-mode outline is guarded today.
* Hidden activities keep their distinct look and a visible edge.
* -Edit mode keeps its existing blue hover outline, unchanged.-

*Section header line*

* Match the subsection chevron to the section chevron: 32×32 with a 16px glyph, not 24×24/14px.
* Centre the chevron, title, badges, action menu and collapse-all on the header line. 

+Presentation only. No behaviour change.+

{panel:bgColor=#fffae6}
*Open question*

Divider colour. MDL-87805 shipped the header/body divider as #e9ecef (border/subtle); Figma uses #dee2e6 (border/default). Which is right, and does the fix belong here or in a follow-up to MDL-87805?
{panel}

h3. How to test

# Course page, not editing — every activity card is grey with a visible border against the grey section body.
# Point at a card — it fills white, the border doesn't change, nothing shifts.
# Tab to a card — grey fill returns, blue border and ring appear, the card doesn't resize and the page doesn't reflow.
# Point at the card you've tabbed to — it stays white.
# Point inside a subsection — only the activity under the pointer changes, not the subsection.
# Hidden activity still reads as hidden and still has an edge.
# -Turn editing on — the blue hover outline behaves as it did before.-
# Section and subsection chevrons are the same size; both header lines are centred.

title: Restyle activity dates as badges
description:
Rescoped. The design has moved on since this ticket was written. Dates use one neutral badge treatment for every type, not colour-coded tags — see the first bullet under Expected behaviour.

h2. Proposed change

Restyle activity dates as badges, and align the dates row with the card's left edge.

Dates currently render as plain text rows. The badge is a small bordered pill with the label and date on one line.

The dates row sits flush with the card's left padding edge, aligned with the title rather than indented to the title text. Two dates sit side by side on one row and wrap together rather than stacking.

No calendar icon, and one treatment for every date type.

h2. User goal

Read an activity's dates as discrete, scannable facts rather than a run of grey text under the description.

h2. Preconditions

* "Show activity dates" is on for the course; test again with it off.
* Test course contains activities covering every shape in the table below, plus one with no dates set.
* Test course has activities inside a subsection as well as directly in a section.
* Contrast is measured against the new fills from [MDL-87833|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87833].

h2. Expected behaviour

On colour: this ticket originally asked for coloured tags with a consistent colour per date type. That is reversed — all date types share one neutral badge. Besides matching the current design, it removes an accessibility problem, since colour-coded date types would need a non-colour carrier as well. The tense of a date is already carried by its label.

The badge has to hold seven date shapes:

||Shape||Example||
|One date|Forum with a due date|
|Two, both past|Choice that has opened and closed|
|Two, both future|Database that has not opened yet|
|Two, mixed tense|Lesson open now and closing later — proof that tense is per date, not per activity|
|Module-specific pair|Assignment, where a submission deadline is not the same as the activity closing|
|Close with no open|Quiz with only a close date set|
|Four dates|Workshop, which contributes the most of any module. They render flat, each carrying its own phase in the label|

* The badge's height is the outer box including its border.
* The label and the date are visibly separated — the gap must be explicit, not inherited from the markup.
* Labels use the existing core date strings. No new strings, no new date sources.
* The label stays programmatically tied to its date, so a screen reader reads "Closes: Monday 26 February" as one phrase.
* Text meets contrast on the grey activity card and on a white subsection header.
* The badge's border is decorative — the badge is understandable without it.
* Test text-spacing overrides explicitly. A fixed badge height is exactly what that breaks.
* At high zoom the row wraps; nothing truncates, clips, or causes the page to scroll sideways.
* No new interactive elements, so no new keyboard or focus requirements.

h2. Test cases

* Each of the seven shapes renders with the right label and tense, including one past and one future badge together on the mixed-tense case.
* Activity with no dates: nothing rendered, no empty container or stray spacing.
* Badge height matches Figma including the border, with a visible gap between label and date.
* Dates row aligns with the card's left padding edge; two dates sit side by side and wrap together.
* "Show activity dates" off: no dates anywhere.
* Text meets contrast on the grey card and inside a subsection.
* High zoom and increased text spacing: wraps, nothing clipped, no sideways page scroll.
* Screen reader reads label and date as one phrase.
* Workshop: all four badges render on one wrapping row, each keeping its own phase label.

h2. Release coordination

Contrast is measured against the fills [MDL-87833|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87833] introduces, so the two release together. Shares spacing with [MDL-89324|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89324] (restriction box), which sits directly below the dates row.

Out of scope: the Figma also shows workshop's four dates wrapped in named groups with the phase prefix dropped from the badges inside. That is not in this ticket. Core's dates API has no grouping concept, so it would need either a new capability there or workshop-specific handling in shared rendering code. Workshop's dates render flat here.

description:

Adding the course title to the sticky header (alongside action and close icons) will improve orientation. h3. 🎯 Technical requirements

* The link should have a subtle hover state (the same as the rest of the elements have now in the course index).
* The title will be positioned at the top of the course index, aligned to the left.
* The action and the close action icons should be moved to the end.
* For long titles, use CSS text-overflow: ellipsis; to prevent the header from expanding vertically or pushing icons off-screen.

* Clicking the title redirects the user to the main course page.

title: Add the react library as an external bundle into core
description:
React will be treated as a platform provided dependency. In this issue we are downloading the relevant react files (react, react-dom/client, jsx-runtime, jsx-dev-runtime) from [https://esm.sh|https://esm.sh]
Ensure that the importmap is updated to point to the locations of these files. Use the code on [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|smart-link] to determine the location. The readme needs to provide full details of how to update the files. Also make sure to add a record in the thirdpartylibs.xml file. This lists all of the third party libraries included in core and their licence.

*Merge Plan*

This issue focuses on the controlled acquisition and serving of the React library. React source files are not exposed as public web assets. They are protected resources served exclusively through the Moodle routing layer.

Instead of placing React files in a publicly accessible folder like {{/lib/javascript.php}}, we will store the "vendored" ESM files in a directory *outside the public web root.*

* *Security:* This prevents direct access to library files outside of the routing layer.
* *Integrity:* Only the Moodle routing system has the permissions to read from this location and serve the content.

Because the files aren't in a public folder, the browser can't "see" them via a standard URL. The router acts as the bridge:

# *Request:* The browser asks for {{react}} via the Import Map.
# *Resolution:* The router maps that request to the internal, non-public file path.
# *Streaming:* The router reads the file and returns it with the appropriate MIME type and cache headers.

This issue includes the tool used to maintain these protected files.

* *Source:* Uses *esm.sh* to pull React and React-DOM in a clean, bundled ESM format. The downloaded files are committed to the repository and are not fetched dynamically at runtime
* *Local Vendoring:* The script downloads the specific, pinned version into the protected internal directory.
* *Verification:* The script can be expanded to verify the integrity of the downloaded files, ensuring the core library hasn't been tampered with.

title: Add the importmaps and other require code to interact with the react build system
description:
Using the code in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|smart-link] as a base, this issue is to include import maps to allow module resolution in the browser. 

The provided patch should also include the alias resolution before file serving.
We have some proof of concept code for using our routing system, and creating a class to handle creating the import map.

When working through this issue, please consider:

* Identify code that is no longer needed
* Remove any experimental scaffolding
* Simplify any code that we put in to produce a working result
* Challenge if each part is needed
* Reduce complexity if possible

Andrew has kindly provided a branch with some code for routing and how to improve the import map code - [https://github.com/andrewnicols/moodle/commits/MDL-87922-main|https://github.com/andrewnicols/moodle/commits/MDL-87922-main|smart-link] 

*Merge Plan*

This issue configures the {{page_requirements_manager}} to generate an Import Map that bridges standard package names to Moodle’s internal routed paths.

Instead of custom internal aliases, we are mapping the official library names directly to our routed resources. This aligns Moodle’s module resolution with standard React package names.

The PHP manager is updated to handle these three distinct types of mappings:

* *Third-Party Core:* Direct mapping for {{react}} (MDL-87908).
* *First-Party Design System:* Direct mapping for {{@moodlehq/design-system}} (MDL-87909).
* *Internal Plugin Logic:* The {{@moodle/lms/}} prefix for all plugin-specific components located in {{[component/path]/js/react/build/}}.

Benefits of using official package names:

* *Standardised Imports:* Developers can use {{import React from 'react'}} instead of a Moodle-specific string.
* *Tooling Alignment:* VS Code and other IDEs can easily resolve these types if the {{tsconfig.json}} is set up to match these mappings, reducing false unresolved module errors in editors
* *Decoupled Delivery Strategy:* If we ever decide to move these libraries to a CDN or a different serving strategy, we only change the URL in the Import Map; we don't have to touch a single line of component code.

title: The PHPUnit GHA workflows are broken
Provide third-party libraries via Composer
description:
h2. What is this issue?

This improvement intends to include all possible third-party libraries using Composer.

Initially this will co-exist with the current approach and we will have them *at the same version as* the versions in Moodle core while we get people used to updating and installing from Composer.

We will also:

* be keeping those dependencies in Moodle until Moodle 6.0.
* only be including those dependencies which have no modifications.
* have to add something to ensure that the {{autoload.files}} are only included if the non-composer version has not already been included (only impacts AWS/SDK).

h2. Why is this important?

This is, essentially, a blocker to the Open Telemetry work because that work will require that some Open Telemetry packages be installed. Some of those Open Telemetry packages will then pull in other dependencies, such as a PSR7 handler, some PSR packages, and more. We already have several of those things and we want to be careful that we don’t end up with _different_ versions included. We want a single source of truth.

h2. Tell me more about versions

Initially we need to make sure that all package versions match the currently installed versions.

When we properly mandate the use of Composer in 6.0, this will need to block the upgrade and installation of Moodle because we have dependencies on things like Mustache.

If we bump any versions of any dependencies we will need to keep them in-sync.

h2. Other things

There are a _couple_ of libraries with local Moodle modifications. For now, we are *_not_* going to include them until we determine the best approach going forward.

We _could_ decide to only do this for the dependencies that we think we are _likely_ to use… but we just don’t know what the limits are there and it seems like a bad idea to me!

The list of modified libraries is currently:

* phpspreadsheet
* xhprof
* php-css-parser (needs major version upgrade)
* google SDK
* scss-php (needs major version upgrade)
* tcpdf

We also exclude our own RTLCSS library because it is heavily dependant upon php-css-parser.

title: Add profiling capability to the react system.
description:
Using the code in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/AE-81|smart-link] Add the additional react files and updates to our system to allow profiling of react components.

Please provide developer documentation

When working through this issue, please consider:

* Identify code that is no longer needed
* Remove any experimental scaffolding
* Simplify any code that we put in to produce a working result
* Challenge if each part is needed
* Reduce complexity if possible

*Merge Plan*

This issue integrates development only profiling into the React lifecycle

* *Automatic Source Discovery:* The profiling logic is baked into the *Auto-init controller (MDL-87765)*. When the Mutation Observer finds a component, it automatically wraps it in a React {{<Profiler>}} during development.
* *Bottleneck Detection:* It tracks {{actualDuration}} (how long a render took) versus {{baseDuration}} (how long it _should_ have taken). This helps identify components with high render costs that may need optimisation.
* *Render Reason Logging:* In development mode, the system can log the cause of a re-render, such as a prop change or a state update triggered by an event.
* *Development performance logging:* Developers receive realtime feedback in the browser console if a component exceeds a "performance budget," helping identify unnecessary or expensive renders during development.
* *Production Safe:* The build system (Esbuild) uses tree-shaking to completely strip this profiling code from production builds, ensuring no profiling code is included in production builds.

title: Wrong version bumping from MDL-83985
description:
[https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|smart-link] introduces wrong version bumpings.

The patch was introduced/rebased shortly after the Moodle 5.0 release to the {{main}} branch of the day. That branch is now the 5.1 branch.

Just before the 5.0 release we perform a version bump for all plugins which increases the version number to the release date, that is {{2025041400}}.

When applying upgrade steps to the {{main}} branch we must always use the current date and this must also be a few days later than the previous release date.

Unforuntately [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|smart-link] did not follow the documented procedures and used a microbump to {{2025041401}} - this fits into the reserved version numberign for the 5.0.x release series. They should have used the “today’s date” of the day, which woudl have beens something like {{2025052200}}

As a result, any change to a plugin on 5.0 which increases the version to a number higher than {{2025041401}} will break all of thse upgrade steps on 5.1 and main. Essentially if we bump the version for any activity plugin on 5.0.x, anyone upgrading from at least that 5.0.x release will not get the 5.1 version bump.

The best fix here is to:

* bump the version.php for all impacted plugins to the _new_ 5.1 release microbump (most of them are {{2025100600}} and will become {{2025100601}}.
* update the {{public/mod/[name]/upgrade.php}} for each to:
** move the step introduced in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-83985|smart-link] to the end fo the function (just before the {{return true;}})
** change the version number in that diffset to the new one we just bumped

We can probably skip this on the {{main}} branch beacuse we haven’t actually bumped any of these plugin’s version numbers _yet_ (I don’t think). If we have then we will need to *copy this step* and bump to *today’s date* but only forthe impacted plugins.

title: cURL security helper method call order check contains a typo
description:
In _(public/)lib/classes/files/curl_security_helper.php,_ the call order check in _get_resolve_info()_ closes the _empty()_ check brackets in the wrong place, which should be corrected.

This does not appear to introduce any obvious security issues because all core flows perform the correct calling order, but this should be fixed on all security supported versions to avoid accidentally introducing any security risks / bypassing any checks in the future.

*Update:* Unit testing the corrected IF statement also uncovered that there were a couple of use cases where the previous implementation worked unexpectedly (threw an exception and rejected the request), because we assumed the hosts, IPs and ports would always be set, and assumed those not being set meant the correct execution order was not performed to check the cURL security config. This was not always true, because some of those values will not be set in cases where no cURL security settings are configured on the site (and therefore no limitations apply). This surfaced since these appear to not be set by default in unit testing.

title: Update security.txt for 5.3 release and related minors
description:
In [MDL-69877] a new security.txt file, following the information @ [security.txt|https://securitytxt.org/] was introduced.

The security.txt file located in _public/security.txt (or security.txt pre 5.1)_ must be updated regularly, shortly before it expires (defined by the {{Expires}} element within the file).

+*The updates should be made to main, as well as all other security supported Moodle versions that contain security.txt.*+ This means all supported versions have an identical security.txt file (including the same expiry).

This task must only land in the minor release versions that are scheduled for release alongside the relevant major release  (for example if 5.3 is the major release, then 5.2.3 will be one of the minors receiving the update, assuming no unscheduled releases have bumped it to 5.2.4 already). Therefore, the ideal window for landing this issue is +2-6 weeks prior to release+.

As a minimum, this will involve updating the {{Expires}} value, which needs to be set to *[expected subsequent major release date]* *+ 3 WEEKS*. This provides a small buffer in case the major release is delayed. If any of other details in the security.txt need to be amended, they should also be completed at the same time. We should also check the RFC in case of any changes (see the [Github repo|https://github.com/securitytxt/security-txt] to check if any versions have been released since the previous LMS release).

----

Detailed information (to be modified for each clone of this issue):

* *Branches affected:* main (5.3), 5.2, 5.1, 5.0, 4.5
* *Expiry (6.0 release + 3 weeks):* 19 April 2027 + 3 week = 10 May 2027
* *Commit message:* MDL-XXXXXX core: Update security.txt expiry
* *Other changes:* _... add any further changes required here_

Exact formatted expiry date to use: *2027-05-10T01:00:00.000Z*

How the date format was calculated (in line with the [latest spec|https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9116#name-expires] - RFC 9116):

{{date --date='10 May 2027 01:00' -u +"%FT%H:%M:%S.000Z"}}

----

(This issue is part of the release process, 2 weeks before release, and will be cloned as part of it.)

title: Footer filtering should not escape content
description:
{{format_string}} escapes content by default, and when [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-85498|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-85498|smart-link] updated the footer to support multi-lang filtering on _$CFG->additionalhtmlfooter_, it didn’t also explicitly declare *not* to escape content, which is a breaking change because it will strip any legitimate scripts added in that admin setting (which would break things like GTM/GA and other site tracking/telemetry that requires a script to be inserted at the bottom of the page, among other things).

This was discovered because it broke the countdown timer on our QA testing site.

title: OpenAI API provider's generate text fails when think tags are present
description:
If you are using "Generate Text" action of an instance of the "OpenAI API provider", the action will fail if the response includes any {{<think>}} tags. The error message under "debuginfo" in the browser console is as follows:

{{Ungültiger Rückgabewert: Invalid external api response: the value is "<think>Okay, the user greeted me in French with "Bonjour gerda, ca va?" which means "Hello Gerda, how are you?" I need to respond in French as per the instructions. Since the user is asking how I am, I should acknowledge their greeting and offer assistance. I should keep it friendly and professional. Let me make sure to use the correct French phrases. I'll say "Bonjour!" to respond to their greeting, then ask how I can assist them today. That should cover it without any markdown or extra formatting.</think>Bonjour ! Comment puis-je vous aider aujourd'hui ?" of PHP type "string", the server was expecting "text" typeError code: invalidresponse}}

If I switch to a model without the {{<think>}} tags the action completes as expected and without error.

The (local) server it is querying is running a OpenWebUI instance which provides an "OpenAI API compatible chat completion endpoint".
I was unable to find out if this a violation of the OpenAI API schema (in that case I'll gladly pester someone else with a bug report in a more relevant project) or something that could happen with the models available at OpenAI as well (I don't use AI outside the locally hosted models at work).

title: Renaming a zip file in the file manager (Private files) throws a TypeError in repository::update_draftfile()
description:
Steps to reproduce:

# Log in as a student and go to Private files in the user menu.
# Click the add button and upload a file.
# Create a folder.
# Move the file into the folder (click on file → change the Path to the new folder).
# Right-click on the folder and press the Zip button.
# Right-click on the resulting zip file, change the name of the file, and click Update.

Expected behaviour:

The zip file is renamed successfully and the updated name is reflected in the file manager.

Actual behaviour:

{noformat}A TypeError exception is thrown:
unserialize_object(): Argument #1 ($input) must be of type string, null given,
called in [dirroot]/repository/lib.php on line 2622
URL: http://localhost/mdk/int_main/user/files.php
Error code: generalexceptionmessage
Stack trace:
line 10190 of /public/lib/moodlelib.php: TypeError thrown
line 2622 of /public/repository/lib.php: call to unserialize_object()
line 147 of /public/repository/draftfiles_ajax.php: call to repository::update_draftfile(){noformat}

Notes:

* Reported by a QA tester in MDLQA-21250 during the Moodle 5.2 QA cycle (MDLQA-21163).
* The update_draftfile() function in repository/lib.php passes a potentially null value to unserialize_object(), which as of PHP 8+ requires the argument to be of type string.
* The issue is specific to renaming a zip file in the file manager; other steps (creating folders, zipping, drag-and-drop upload) work as expected.

title: Single quotes in search query return no results on MSSQL (non full-text fallback path)
description:
h3. Summary

When using the Simple search engine ({{search_simpledb}}) on a site where {{is_fulltext_search_supported()}} returns false (e.g. MSSQL without full-text search installed), searching for a term containing a single quote (e.g. it's) returns no results.

!Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 18-37-50 Global search int_nftss.png|width=250!

Single quotes

!Screenshot 2026-04-13 at 18-38-04 Global search int_nftss.png|width=250!

Double quotes

h3. Root Cause

In {{search/engine/simpledb/classes/engine.php}}, the {{get_simple_query()}} method only strips double quotes from the query string before building the LIKE-based SQL:

{noformat}$q = str_replace('"', '', $q);{noformat}

Single quotes are left untouched, which causes the LIKE '%it's%' parameter to effectively break on MSSQL, silently returning no results.

h3. Steps to Reproduce

# Set up a Moodle site on MSSQL without full-text search enabled
# Enable global search with Simple search engine
# Index some content
# Search for a term containing a single quote (e.g. it's or Moodle's)
# Observe: no results returned

h3. Expected Behaviour

Search results containing the term should be returned, with the single quote either stripped or properly handled.

h3. Suggested Fix

In get_simple_query(), also strip single quotes:

{noformat}> $q = str_replace(['"', "'"], '', $q);{noformat}

title: Bump all versions, requires and dependencies near the 5.2 release
description:
This task corresponds to point #3 of the [1 week prior release|https://moodledev.io/general/development/process/release#1-week-prior] tasks.

It's achieved semi-automatically using the "{{versions_check_set.sh}}" script available in the [local_ci|https://github.com/moodlehq/moodle-local_ci/blob/main/versions_check_set/versions_check_set.sh] plugin.

# Create a working {{main}} instance local_ci plugin installed. Remove Composer's "vendor" directory and any non-core plugins if you're working on an existing instance.

# Define and export all the env variables required by the script.

* {{$WORKSPACE}}: Path to the directory where test results will be sent ({{/tmp}})
* {{$phpcmd}}: Path to the PHP CLI executable (e.g. {{/usr/bin/php}})
* {{$gitdir}}: Directory containing git repo (the dirroot of the git, working site)
* {{$setversion}}: 10digits (YYYYMMDD00) to set all versions to. Empty = not set. Since Moodle 2.7, it has been agreed to bump to the planned release version for easier automated checks later in stable land.
* {{$setrequires}}: 10 digits (YYYYMMDD00) to set all required values. Empty = default to $setversion. Since Moodle 2.7, it has been agreed to perform the required bump to the current master version (usually an RC one).

# Run the "{{versions_check_set.sh}}" script. If there are errors, they will be reported, and fixing them will be necessary. (look for "{{ERROR}}" in the {{$WORKSPACE/versions_check_set.txt}} file and/or check the exit status of the script)

# Without errors, all the versions, requires, and dependencies will be bumped.

# Commit

# Note that the main version file is NOT updated at all. One extra commit bumping may be necessary (to anything >= requires version).

# Rerun the checker to verify that there are no errors and no more changes are performed.

Note that the checker is also run periodically by the CI server and as part of the "remote_branch_checker," so normally, all the version.php files should be under control.

(This issue will be cloned for each major release).

Ciao 🙂

title: Add Moodle 5.2.0 upgrade line to all the upgrade.php scripts
description:
To have it properly detected for the future, it would be great to add to all the upgrade.php scripts some lines like these:

{code:php}// Automatically generated Moodle v5.2.0 release upgrade line.
// Put any upgrade step following this.{code}

exactly before the "{{return true;}}" present in all the scripts.

Normally, it's ok to do that both in the stable (502_STABLE) and the {{main}} branches, so they will allow quickly find where 5.2.0 started and act once we decide future requirements.

But, *when under parallel development, this only can be done in the stable (502_STABLE) branch* as the {{main}} branch already has diverged and can have own upgrade steps not corresponding to the version just released, but to the future version being developed in parallel.

The change can be performed globally with:

{code:java}#!/bin/bash
export rel="5.2.0" && find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | \
grep '/db/' | \
xargs grep -L "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
xargs perl -p -i -e 's@( *)(return true;)@\1// Automatically generated Moodle v$ENV{rel} release upgrade line.\n\1// Put any upgrade step following this.\n\n\1\2@s'{code}

*Command to detect* all the upgrade.php files not having those lines:

{code:java}find . -name upgrade.php | xargs grep -l 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade' | grep '/db/' | xargs grep -L 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.2.0 release upgrade'{code}

*Commands to detect* that we have not added the lines to incorrect files:

{code:java}grep -lr 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.2.0 release upgrade' * | grep -v '/db/'
grep -lr 'Automatically generated Moodle v5.2.0 release upgrade' * | xargs grep -L 'function.*xmldb_.*_upgrade'{code}

*Command to detect* if the lines have been added after a post-release upgrade step. If there are upgrade steps found, verify that all of them were already there the day of the release and have not been introduced later (you can look for differences between the release v5.2.0 and the current {{main}} branch to verify that)

{code:java}export rel="5.2.0" && export ver="202604" &&
find . -name upgrade.php | \
xargs grep -B25 "Automatically generated Moodle v${rel} release upgrade" | \
grep "upgrade_.*_savepoint.*${ver}"{code}

*Important note to integrators*: The sooner this issue is integrated after release, the fewer chances to get the lines put in an incorrect place (that's what the last "command to detect" above tries to avoid. We need to ensure that the lines are *exactly* at the release point (or we may end up deleting upgrade steps incorrectly in the future). So, immediate integration after release (within the on-sync period and ideally before any new upgrade step is added), it the best achievement.

Ciao 🙂

title: Create UI for OAuth 2 Login flows
description:
h3. Summary

Create the User Interface for the OAuth2 Server user authorisation workflow. This covers three screens, plus a refactor to share common logic between them.

This is UI/rendering work only. Wiring these screens into the actual OAuth2 authorisation route/controller (parent epic MDL-87215) is out of scope here.

There is no existing UX/Figma mockup to follow. Visual design should follow the existing login page's style and components, reusing the same page layout/branding (site logo, background, language menu, maintenance banner) for all three screens so the flow feels consistent.

h3. Screens

*1. Login screen (existing, to be updated)*

* This is today's Moodle login screen ({{core_auth\output\login}}), shown when the user isn't already logged in.
* It should additionally display the requesting OAuth2 client's identity (name, logo/icon, link to the client's website) so the user knows what they're logging in for _before_ entering credentials.

*2. "Continue as [user]" screen (new)*

* Shown when the user is already logged in.
* Displays the current user's name and profile picture, and asks them to confirm they want to continue as that user.
* Displays the requesting client's identity (name, logo/icon, link to website) for the same trust/verification reasons as the login screen.
* Includes a "Not you? Log in as a different user" option, which logs the current user out and shows the login screen instead.

*3. Scope confirmation screen (new)*

* Lists the scopes being requested, each with a brief description.
* Where the client has previously been granted some scopes by this user and is now requesting more, the screen distinguishes between:
** _Already granted_ scopes (shown informationally)
** _Newly requested_ scopes (require the user's consent)
* Displays the requesting client's identity (name, logo/icon, link to website).
* Approval is _all-or-nothing_ — the user cannot selectively approve/deny individual scopes. They either approve the full set of newly-requested scopes, or cancel.

h3. Shared behaviour across all screens

* *Decline/Cancel*: clicking Cancel/Deny on the continue-as-user or scope-confirmation screen redirects back to the client's {{redirect_uri}} with a standard OAuth2 {{error=access_denied}} response, per spec. No Moodle-side "access denied" page.
* *Silent re-authorisation*: if a logged-in user re-authorises a client for scopes they've already fully granted (no new scopes requested), the continue-as-user and scope-confirmation screens should be skipped — but the current user's name and profile image should still be shown briefly/contextually as part of that flow, so it's clear who is continuing.
* Shared rendering logic (error/info messages, maintenance banner, language menu, etc.) currently embedded in {{core_auth\output\login}} should be extracted into a reusable trait so it can be shared across the login, continue-as-user, and scope-confirmation renderables without duplication.

h3. Out of scope / not included

* Behat acceptance test coverage — not currently feasible to validate an OAuth2 flow end-to-end in Behat; test coverage will need to be addressed separately (e.g. via unit/JS tests where practical).
* Wiring these renderables into the OAuth2 authorisation route/controller (tracked under the parent epic/other tickets).

h3. Notes

A proof-of-concept branch exists (MDL-87215-main) with a rough sketch of a shared {{login_renderable_trait}} and {{core_auth\output\oauth2\confirm_scopes}} / {{continue_as_user}} renderables. This PoC is exploratory only and does _not_ represent the agreed design — it should inform, not dictate, the implementation of this ticket.

title: Implement token revocation endpoints and logic
description:
Develop endpoints and backend logic to allow revocation of access tokens, authorization codes, and refresh tokens. Ensure revocation is immediate and properly invalidates tokens across the system.

h2. Approach

Implement a single, unified {{/revoke}} endpoint per RFC 7009 (OAuth 2.0 Token Revocation), rather than separate endpoints per token type. The endpoint accepts {{token}} and {{token_type_hint}} parameters and always returns HTTP 200, even for already-invalid or unknown tokens, to avoid leaking token validity to attackers.

h2. Authentication & authorization

* Confidential clients must authenticate to call {{/revoke}}.
* Public clients are not required to authenticate, but the token being revoked must be verified as belonging to the calling {{client_id}} before it is revoked (prevents a client revoking another client's token).

h2. Cascading revocation

* Revoking a refresh token must cascade: all access tokens issued from that refresh token are invalidated in the same operation, fully cutting off the client's access.
* Revoking an access token or authorization code only invalidates that specific token.

h2. Enforcement mechanism

Because access tokens may be JWTs (stateless), a revocation/denylist table must be maintained and checked on every authenticated API request so that revocation takes effect immediately, rather than relying on short token lifetimes alone.

h2. Scope boundaries

* In scope: the client-facing {{/revoke}} endpoint and its backend revocation logic (self-service revocation by the token owner).
* Out of scope: admin-initiated bulk revocation UI/flows (e.g. an admin revoking all tokens for a user or client) — this belongs to the OAuth2 Server administration UI tickets (MDL-88468, MDL-88474), which can call into this backend logic later.

h2. Dependencies

* *Blocked by MDL-89181* (Implement OAuth2 Server client manager class) — needed to resolve/validate the client_id and enforce token-ownership checks for public clients.
* *Related to MDL-89089* (Implement OAuth2 Server Scope repository layer) — in progress; not a hard blocker, but scopes tied to revoked tokens should be considered during implementation.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# {{/revoke}} endpoint implemented per RFC 7009 semantics (always 200, {{token}} + {{token_type_hint}} params).
# Client authentication enforced for confidential clients; token-ownership verified for public clients.
# Revoking a refresh token cascades to invalidate its associated access tokens.
# Revoked tokens are rejected by resource server checks immediately (via revocation/denylist table), not just after natural expiry.
# PHPUnit test coverage for: valid revocation, invalid/unknown token (still 200), foreign-token rejection, and cascading revocation.

----

Create CLI tooling for React component swizzling
description:
Implement CLI tooling that allows developers to discover and scaffold React component overrides in Moodle themes and plugins.

The initial implementation should be written in JavaScript and integrated with Moodle's existing JavaScript CLI tooling.

h2. Features

h3. Component discovery

The CLI should provide an interactive search experience for discovering React components that can be overridden.

Initially, the search should be limited to {{.tsx}} files within the Moodle codebase.

h3. Component support status

Each discovered component should display a theming support status:

* {{safe}} - explicitly supported for theming
* {{risky}} - theming is allowed, but compatibility is not guaranteed
* {{prohibited}} - should not be themed

If no support metadata exists for a component, the CLI should default to {{risky}}.

Components marked as {{prohibited}} must not be generated by the tooling.

The status names are still up for debate

h3. Override generation

Once a component has been selected, the CLI should generate the appropriate override file in the target theme or plugin.

The generated file should contain scaffold code that allows developers to immediately begin customisation without manually creating the file structure or determining import paths.

h3. Wrap mode

Wrap mode should generate a component that imports and renders the original component, providing a safe extension point for additional behaviour or presentation changes.

h3. Target selection

Before generating an override, the CLI should determine the target theme or plugin.

When the command is executed from the Moodle root directory, the developer should be prompted to select the target theme or plugin from the available candidates.

When the command is executed from within a supported theme or plugin directory, the target may be inferred automatically.

h3. Override mode

Once a component and target have been selected, the CLI should generate the appropriate override file in the target theme or plugin.

The generated file should contain scaffold code that allows developers to immediately begin customisation without manually creating the file structure or determining import paths.

h2. Out of scope

The definition of component support metadata, metadata file format, and classification of components should be tracked separately. This issue focuses on the CLI workflow and code generation.

Until metadata support is implemented, components without metadata should be treated as {{risky}}.

title: Forum: Replace discussion navigation links with icon buttons
description:
The current navigation between forum discussions utilises text-based "Next" and "Previous" links at the bottom of the page. While functional, this pattern is dated and consumes significant vertical space:

!Screenshot from 2026-04-30 11-35-05-20260430-093505.png|width=600,alt="Screenshot from 2026-04-30 11-35-05-20260430-093505.png"!

Modern Moodle UI components are shifting towards compact icon-based navigation (arrow buttons). By moving to icon buttons, we improve the visual hierarchy and ensure that navigation controls are easily identifiable without cluttering the interface with redundant text:

!image-20260430-095652.png|width=600,alt="image-20260430-095652.png"!

h3. 🎯 Required actions

* Update the templates to replace the text-link elements with chevron-style arrow buttons. Ensure the buttons are grouped correctly at the top and bottom of the discussion view as per the prototype.
* Ensure the existing logic correctly populates the button properties, including title attributes for tooltips to maintain context.
* Verify that the icon buttons provide sufficient touch targets for mobile users and align correctly within the action bar's flex container.
* When the "Experimental nested discussion view" setting is enabled, discussion navigation shouldn't be displayed (as currently happens).
* Ensure that while the text is visually removed, the aria-label or title attributes explicitly state "Previous discussion: [Title]" and "Next discussion: [Title]" for screen reader users.

h3. (/) Acceptance criteria

* The text-based links for discussion navigation are replaced by chevron icon buttons.
* Navigation buttons appear in the top-end and bottom-end of the discussion view, matching the provided mockup.
* Hovering over an icon button reveals a tooltip with the title of the target discussion ("Previous discussion: [Title]" and "Next discussion: [Title]").
* The navigation remains functional, respecting forum visibility settings and group restrictions.
* The buttons are appropriately disabled (greyed out) or hidden if no previous or next discussion exists.
* The discussion navigation arrows are not displayed when the "Experimental nested discussion view" user preference is enabled.
* The implementation uses standard Moodle icon components.

title: Forum: Add "Go to all discussions" link to the sticky footer

Introducing a "Go to all discussions" link within the sticky footer provides a centralised navigation point that remains accessible regardless of the discussion length. !image-20260430-105638.png|width=600,alt="image-20260430-105638.png"!

* Update the core footer logic to ensure that this supplementary information is rendered even if linear navigation is disabled or unavailable for a specific activity instance.
* Update {{mod_forum}} to utilise this new API, passing the "Go to all discussions" link to the sticky footer.
* Add the {{gotoalldiscussions}} string to the {{mod_forum.php}} language file.

The implementation should follow the approach established in the [linked PoC|https://github.com/sarjona/moodle/commit/MDL-87302-main-poc], specifically focusing on the following areas:

* Clicking the link successfully redirects the user to the main forum page (view.php).

title: Navigation footer: Implement linear navigation exceptions for Previous/Next
description:

Specifically, we need to handle the start of course sections and the end of the course. At the first activity of a course, the “Previous” link should be suppressed to encourage a forward-moving flow within that module. At the final activity of the entire course, the “Next” link should be replaced with a clear "Back to course" link to return the user to the main course page for closure:

This issue tracks the implementation of an exception rule to suppress the sticky footer rendering for the *Choice* activity during specific interaction and administrative states. While the linear navigation footer is beneficial for progression between activities, it can interfere with the user's focus when they are actively selecting or when teachers are managing responses.

The footer should be suppressed in management views to provide a clean interface for data review.

h3. 🎯 *Required action*

* Suppress the footer rendering logic for the following cases:
** *Response reports*: {{report.php}} (where teachers view the list of respondents and their selections).
** *Administrative views*: Any pages related to permissions, logs, or backup/restore within the activity context.
* Maintain footer visibility for the following student-facing states:
** When the student is viewing options to "Save my choice".
** When the student is viewing the results graph or confirmation of their selection.

h3. (/) *Acceptance criteria*

* The sticky footer is *visible* to students on the main Choice page ({{view.php}}), both when they are making a selection and after they have submitted it.
* The sticky footer is *hidden automatically* when a teacher or manager is viewing the "Responses" report page.
* The sticky footer is *hidden* during administrative tasks (e.g., editing permissions, viewing logs, or backup/restore).
* No console errors are triggered by the "missing" footer component on these excluded administrative pages.
* The user experience remains consistent with the provided prototypes, where course navigation remains persistent for the learner's primary interaction with the activity

title: Navigation footer: Add exceptions for the Database linear navigation
description:

title: Phpunit and behat fails if a plugin registers own autoloader
description:
Phpunit fails when there’s a plugin in the code base that registers its own autoloader in lib.php.

Not sure if this is a real “bug” in the moodle core code or if plugins just should not do something like requiring an own autoloader in the lib.php file. Anyway, plugins might do this, even if it is discouraged, so it makes sense to harden the core code to deal with these cases.

To reproduce:

* git clone [https://github.com/owncloud/moodle-repository_ocis|https://github.com/owncloud/moodle-repository_ocis|smart-link]  public/repository/ocis
* cd public/repository/ocis
* git checkout 42c7f34ab959af0788100ea00113fd6726129f30
* rm phpunit.xml (if exists)
* php public/admin/tool/phpunit/cli/util.php --drop (important and necessary, because afterwards, “allversionshash” cannot be read from config table which then forces caches to be rebuilt and load all plugins' lib.php files (including the one with the autoload require of repository_ocis.
* php public/admin/tool/phpunit/init.php
* Verify that phpunit.xml has NOT been created in content root, instead it has been built in public/repository/ocis
* When now running phpunit the phpunit.xml is not being found and an error occurs.

Similar issues will properly occur, if some autoloading is being done inside some autoloaded classes.

This also probably only happens, because repository_ocis registers itself with `$loader->register(true);` (repository/ocis/vendor/composer/autoload_real.php#34) which registers itself before the moodle root loader.
In {{InstalledVersions::getInstalled()::getRootPackage()}} the value {{$installed[0]}} then is not the moodle core loader but the repository_ocis one and phpunit.xml ends up being written to the wrong path.

So summing it up:

* Mainly, repository_ocis is doing a lot of bad things that lead to this issue. One could argue that this has to be fixed in the plugin.
* However, on the other hand, with the introduction of composer more and more plugins will continue to introduce composer and it’s maybe just a matter of time until there will be more plugins causing trouble.
* So I suggest to harden the core code to deal with such kind of things.

title: Allow specific file extensions to be allowed through ESM loader
description:
Some ESM bundles we want to load include the {{.js}} extension, for example Bootstrap’s {{bootstrap.js}} index looks like:


{code:javascript}export { default as Alert } from './src/alert.js'
export { default as Button } from './src/button.js'
export { default as Carousel } from './src/carousel.js'
export { default as Collapse } from './src/collapse.js'
export { default as Dropdown } from './src/dropdown.js'
export { default as Modal } from './src/modal.js'
export { default as Offcanvas } from './src/offcanvas.js'
export { default as Popover } from './src/popover.js'
export { default as ScrollSpy } from './src/scrollspy.js'
export { default as Tab } from './src/tab.js'
export { default as Toast } from './src/toast.js'
export { default as Tooltip } from './src/tooltip.js'{code}

Our current loader would require us to modify each of these includes to remove the {{.js}} in each of the export from statements.

So instead of automatically loading the {{.js}} file by automatically adding the suffix, the idea here is to allow the URL to include _certain_ suffixes, notably:

* {{.js}}

At the same time, by allowing {{.js.map}} we can also support source maps.

However, if it is included with other search/filtering-related controls, such as in the “Course overview” block, which also defines a search landmark for the container that contains the filtering and search controls. title: Generate development and production outputs for ESM code
description:
Initially we went with a single build for the ESM outputs. In [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88786|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88786|smart-link] we simplified this build because it was generating different output depending on whether the build was run in watch mode or not - the watch would generate a ‘dev' build with some different options for minify, sourcemapping, etc.

Now we know we do not want a different built depending on how the code is built, but this did later raise the question of whether we wanted a dev build at all.

In our YUI days we generated three outputs:

* min.js - a minified version for production
* .js - a non-minified version for …????
* -debug.js - a non-minified version with debugging

We did away with this with AMD.

And now I feel like we should come back to it with our new React overlord as it has a number of benefits when it comes to React client-side tooling and management.

The advantages as I see it:

* React profiler can be enabled/disabled based on the version used
* Source maps can be provided to clients for Development only
* Various other development features can be enabled for development, including:
** jsxDev
** keepNames
** minify



Whilst an improvement we shoudl still backport this change, which is in keeping with the policy we have for AMD changes. I don’t anticipate many people using ESM in 5.2, but it is still supported.

I would also suggest that we rename the task from {{grunt react}} to {{grunt esm}} given this is not a react-specific task.

title: Backup file_logger should store relative paths
description:
h2. Summary

Backup {{file_logger}} should serialize a relative path (just the filename) rather than the absolute {{$CFG->backuptempdir/$backupid.log}}. 

The absolute path is host specific and ends up baked into the backup controller record and into the {{.mbz}} artefact, which makes backups non portable and causes restore code to blindly open whatever path was deserialized. title: Performance regression after implementing MDL-60912
description:
MDL-60912 (integrated in 5.0.7 / 5.1.4 / main) changed \core_completion\progress::get_course_progress_percentage() to call the new completion_info::get_user_activities_with_completion() instead of the lightweight get_activities().


For every course module with completion enabled, get_user_activities_with_completion() now constructs a \core_availability\info_module and calls filter_user_list(), which in turn calls capability_checker::get_users_by_capability('moodle/course:ignoreavailabilityrestrictions') on the module context.


This availability + capability resolution runs per module, per course, per request. On pages that summarise many courses via course_summary_exporter — Dashboard, Calendar block, Timeline block, Starred courses, My overview — the cost multiplies (courses × completion-enabled modules × capability resolution) and produces a noticeable performance regression compared with 5.0.6. The expensive work is also repeated because get_course_progress_percentage() is called multiple times per request for the same (course, user) pair (e.g. calendar/classes/external/event_exporter_base.php instantiates a new course_summary_exporter per event).


+*_This was anticipated during the MDL-60912 review (performance concern was raised in the comments) but no follow-up optimisation was integrated._*+



*Steps to reproduce*

# Site with completion tracking enabled.
# A user enrolled in many courses, each with several completion-tracked activities (with few or no availability/group restrictions — the common case).
# Load the Dashboard (or a page with the Calendar / Timeline / Starred courses blocks).
# Profile the request (e.g. $CFG->perfdebug = 15, or an APM/DB-query profiler).

Expected result
Course progress percentages are calculated with overhead comparable to 5.0.6; unrestricted activities do not incur per-module availability/capability resolution.


*Actual result*
Each completion-tracked module triggers an info_module + get_users_by_capability() resolution, repeated across courses and repeated per call within the same request, measurably increasing DB load and page render time.


*Affected code*

* completion/classes/progress.php — get_course_progress_percentage()
* lib/completionlib.php — get_user_activities_with_completion() (introduced by MDL-51447, used by MDL-60912)
* Callers via core_course\external\course_summary_exporter (Dashboard, block_calendar_*, block_timeline, block_starredcourses, block_myoverview, enrol/externallib.php, report builder completion formatter)



*Proposed solution*
Two complementary, behaviour-preserving optimisations (correctness of MDL-60912 fully retained):

# Fast path in get_user_activities_with_completion() — when a module has no availability rule (empty($cm->availability)), is not in separate-groups mode ($cm->groupmode !== SEPARATEGROUPS), and has no grouping restriction (empty($cm->groupingid)), the module is accessible to every enrolled user. Skip the info_module + capability_checker work and count it directly. This is mathematically equivalent to the existing slow path for unrestricted modules (the overwhelming majority). Modules that actually carry a restriction still take the full slow path, so hidden/unavailable/group-restricted activities continue to be excluded correctly.
# Per-request memoisation in get_course_progress_percentage() — cache the computed percentage per (course, user) in a MODE_REQUEST cache so repeated calls within one request (multiple exporters) reuse the result. Cheap pre-checks (is_enabled(), is_tracked_user()) stay outside the cache so capability/setting changes are always honoured. The cache key embeds $course->cacherev (so structural / visibility / availability / grouping changes invalidate it automatically), and the cache is purged in completion_info::internal_set_data() so completion-state changes within the same request are reflected.
No DB schema change, no version.php bump, no new cache definition, no new events/observers required.

Steps to reproduce

# Site with completion tracking enabled.
# A user enrolled in many courses, each with several completion-tracked activities (with few or no availability/group restrictions — the common case).
# Load the Dashboard (or a page with the Calendar / Timeline / Starred courses blocks).
# Profile the request (e.g. $CFG->perfdebug = 15, or an APM/DB-query profiler).



*At Moxis, we have already implemented a fix and it works. It keeps the fix from MDL-60912 but skips unnecessary steps and caches where relevant. I have added the patch for this issue as an attachment.*

title: Course index subsections expose duplicate treeitem roles
description:
Problem statement:
Subsections in the course index currently expose a nested treeitem role. The wrapper for a subsection is exposed as a treeitem even though its parent course-index list item already represents that same subsection as a treeitem. This can cause assistive technologies to perceive two tree nodes for one visible subsection.

This affects people who navigate the course index with assistive technology, particularly screen-reader users. It does not provide a clear, programmatically determinable representation of the subsection as required by WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 4.1.2, Name, Role, Value (Level A).

Current behaviour:
- A visible subsection can be represented by nested elements that both expose role="treeitem".
- Assistive technology may announce or expose duplicate tree nodes for one subsection.
- The attached reference image, MDL-88949-current-behaviour.png, reproduces the duplicate role in the current Moodle main behaviour.

Reference image captured from current behaviour:
!MDL-88949-current-behaviour.png!

Expected behaviour:
- Each visible subsection is exposed as one course-index tree node with one treeitem role.
- The subsection tree node has the correct accessible name.
- Expandable subsection nodes expose the correct expanded or collapsed state.
- Course-index keyboard navigation and subsection expand/collapse behaviour continue to work.

Value:
The course index will expose an unambiguous structure to assistive technologies. Screen-reader users will encounter one meaningful tree node per visible subsection and receive the correct name and state information.

Scope:
In scope:
- The semantic representation of subsection entries in the course index.
- Subsection accessible names, expanded/collapsed states, and existing keyboard interaction as affected by this correction.

Out of scope:
- Other course-index item types.
- The content and presentation of the subsection page itself.
- Unrelated changes to course-index navigation or visual design.

Acceptance criteria:
- A subsection is represented by exactly one treeitem in the browser accessibility tree.
- The subsection treeitem has an accessible name that identifies the subsection.
- A subsection that can expand or collapse exposes the correct aria-expanded state, and that state updates when the subsection is expanded or collapsed.
- Keyboard navigation through the course index continues to include each subsection once and remains functional.
- A screen reader does not announce two tree nodes for a single visible subsection.
- The correction applies whether the subsection is expanded or collapsed and whether it contains course activities.
- Existing course-index display and interaction for subsection entries are unchanged visually.
- Other course-index item types continue to behave as before.

References:
- WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 4.1.2, Name, Role, Value: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/name-role-value.html
- WAI-ARIA Tree View Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/
- Current-behaviour reproduction and Firefox DOM evidence: MDL-88949-current-behaviour.png, attached to this issue.

Notes:
The required outcome is one programmatically exposed tree node per visible subsection. The ticket intentionally does not prescribe which HTML element must carry the treeitem role; implementation should follow the established course-index pattern while producing the required accessibility-tree result.
