title: Assignment grading: Sticky table header is misplaced at 400% zoom
description:
Summary:    
At 400% browser zoom and a very short viewport, the sticky header in the assignment submissions grading table stays pinned after the primary navbar is no longer fixed. This leaves a large sticky header consuming much of the viewport, so only a small strip remains for the submission rows.

Problem statement:    
Teachers reviewing assignment submissions at high zoom can lose usable space for the grading table. The problem occurs when the effective viewport is both narrower than 576 CSS pixels and 320 CSS pixels high or less. At this size, the primary navbar is no longer fixed, creating additional vertical space, but the sticky grading-table header keeps occupying a large part of the viewport. Combined with the page sticky footer, very little of the submission table body remains visible.

This is an accessibility defect affecting users who rely on browser zoom and small effective viewports. It relates to WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 1.4.10 Reflow (Level AA):  
[https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html](https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html)

Current behaviour:

* At 400% zoom, with window.innerWidth at or below 576 pixels and window.innerHeight at or below 320 pixels, the primary navbar is no longer fixed.
* The assignment submissions grading-table header stays sticky and continues to occupy a large part of the small viewport.
* As the teacher scrolls vertically, the sticky header keeps consuming viewport height that is needed for the submission rows.
* When the page sticky footer is also shown, barely any of the submission table body remains readable.
* See the attached reference mockup image image-20260626-041105.png, which must remain attached to this issue.

Expected behaviour:

* When the primary navbar is no longer fixed at the affected viewport size, the assignment submissions grading-table header becomes non-sticky (position: static) so it no longer consumes a large part of the available viewport.
* The header scrolls together with the submission rows, like an ordinary table header, instead of remaining pinned.
* Submission rows remain readable and are not reduced to a small strip beneath a sticky header, including when the page sticky footer is shown.
* Horizontal and vertical scrolling remain available so all grading-table content can be reached at 400% zoom.
* At viewport sizes above the affected breakpoint, the header keeps its normal sticky behaviour.

Value:

Teachers using high browser zoom can read assignment submission data without a sticky header consuming a substantial part of the available viewport. This supports reflow accessibility requirements.

Scope:    
In scope:

* The sticky header used by the assignment submissions grading table.
* Behaviour when the primary navbar is no longer fixed at the affected effective viewport dimensions.
* Equivalent fixes on main, Moodle 5.2, Moodle 5.1, and Moodle 4.5.

Out of scope:

* Sticky headers outside the assignment submissions grading table.
* General redesign of Moodle responsive navigation.
* Changes to assignment grading workflows unrelated to the sticky-header position.

Acceptance criteria:

* At 400% browser zoom, when window.innerWidth is at or below 576 pixels and window.innerHeight is at or below 320 pixels, the assignment submissions grading-table header is non-sticky (position: static) after the primary navbar is no longer fixed, so it does not consume a large part of the viewport.
* At this viewport size the header scrolls with the submission rows rather than remaining pinned.
* Submission rows remain readable and are not left in a small strip beneath a sticky header, including when the page sticky footer is shown.
* All grading-table content remains reachable using horizontal and vertical scrolling.
* Behaviour at viewport dimensions above the affected breakpoint does not regress; the header remains sticky with its normal offset.
* The fix is verified on main, Moodle 5.2, Moodle 5.1, and Moodle 4.5.

Attachments and references:

* image-20260626-041105.png is the reference mockup demonstrating the defect and must remain attached.
* backup-moodle2-course-3-cc101-20250504-0144.mbz provides a course with multiple submissions for testing.
* In the restored course, use the assignment named Cloud-Based Application Design and Deployment.
* Source: 2026 WCAG accessibility audit.

title: Accessibility issues with the custom fields admin pages
description:
Summary:
Ensure that adding a custom field category produces an accessible status message.

Problem statement:
When an administrator adds a category on either of the reported custom fields administration pages, Moodle displays confirmation of the result visually, but the message is not programmatically exposed as a status message. Screen reader users therefore receive no feedback that the category was added.

This affects administrators and other authorised users who use screen readers or comparable assistive technologies.

Current behaviour:
Activating "Add a new category" adds the category and displays visual feedback. Assistive technology does not announce the result.

The problem occurs on:
- Site administration > Courses > Default settings > Course custom fields
- Site administration > General > Custom fields > Shared custom fields

Expected behaviour:
After "Add a new category" is activated, the result is programmatically determinable as a status message and can be announced by assistive technologies without the message receiving focus.

The announcement must provide enough context for the user to understand that a category was added. The existing visual experience must remain available.

Value:
Screen reader users receive equivalent confirmation of the result of their action and can continue working without searching the page for an unannounced change. This addresses WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 4.1.3 Status Messages (Level AA).

Scope:
In scope:
- The result of activating "Add a new category" on the Course custom fields administration page.
- The result of activating "Add a new category" on the Shared custom fields administration page.
- Programmatic exposure of the result to assistive technologies.
- Preservation of the existing visual feedback and category-creation behaviour.

Out of scope:
- Other custom field actions, including editing, deleting, reordering, or moving categories or fields.
- Other administration pages.
- General redesign of custom field management.

Acceptance criteria:
- Activating "Add a new category" successfully creates a category on each of the two reported pages.
- The resulting confirmation is programmatically determinable as a status message through an appropriate role or property.
- Assistive technology can announce the complete, meaningful result without focus being moved to the message.
- The message does not use an unnecessarily interruptive alert mechanism for routine success feedback.
- Existing visual confirmation remains visible.
- Existing keyboard focus and category-management behaviour do not regress.

Accessibility reference:
WCAG 2.2 SC 4.1.3 Status Messages:
https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/status-messages.html

Notes:
WCAG identifies a success or result message which does not change context as a status message. Its sufficient techniques include exposing routine success feedback using role="status". Equivalent conforming implementations are acceptable; the requirement is the observable and programmatic accessibility outcome, not a prescribed implementation.

title: Accessibility issues in Comments
description:
Problem statement

The core comments component (public/comment/comment.js) has two categories of WCAG 2.2 non-compliance affecting all users who post or interact with comments across Moodle.


Colour contrast (SC 1.4.3 Contrast Minimum, Level AA)

1. New comment highlight -- when a comment is submitted, a YUI2 animation permanently sets the newly posted comment's background colour to #FFE390 (yellow) and the text/link colour to #06e (blue). The measured contrast ratio of #0066EE against #FFE390 is 4.02:1, below the required 4.5:1 minimum for normal-weight text. Any grey meta text rendered over the same yellow background has a contrast ratio of only 3.13:1. The yellow background persists indefinitely after the animation completes.

The attached screenshots show both issues in context.

User link on yellow background: !image-20260625-085115.png|thumbnail!

Comment date and text on yellow background: !image-20260625-085132.png|thumbnail!

2. Simulated placeholder text -- the comment textarea uses a JavaScript placeholder simulation (toggle_textarea in comment.js) that sets the textarea value to the string "Add a comment" and styles it with colour grey (#808080). The contrast ratio of #808080 against a white background is 3.95:1, below the 4.5:1 minimum.


Use of colour (SC 1.4.1, Level A)

The animation at comment.js line 107 sets the colour of the entire newly posted comment list item -- including both the username anchor element and the surrounding non-link text -- to #06e. Because both link and non-link content receive the same colour, and no independent non-colour visual indicator (such as an underline) is separately enforced for the link in that state, colour becomes the only visual means of distinguishing the username link from surrounding text.


Current behaviour

When a comment is posted, the new list item permanently receives background #FFE390 and text/link colour #06e via a YUI2 ColorAnim call. The textarea placeholder is simulated by setting its value to the "Add a comment" string in grey. Neither colour choice meets WCAG 2.2 Level AA contrast requirements. The username link is not visually distinguishable from surrounding text during the highlighted state.


Expected behaviour

All text and interactive controls within the comments component must meet SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) AA (4.5:1 for normal-weight text). The username link must have a non-colour visual indicator. The textarea placeholder text must be implemented in a way that meets contrast requirements.


WCAG references

- SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) Level AA: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/contrast-minimum.html
- SC 1.4.1 Use of Color Level A: https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG21/Understanding/use-of-color.html


Design system tokens

The Moodle Design System (@moodlehq/design-system) does not include a direct equivalent to #FFE390. The closest available semantic token for a new-item highlight background is:

- $mds-bg-feedback-warning-subtle: #fcefdc (contrast 7.82:1 with $mds-text-feedback-warning, 14.28:1 with $mds-text-default, 4.73:1 with $mds-text-link-primary-default -- all pass AA)

For the placeholder text, suitable tokens include:

- $mds-text-subtle: #495057 (contrast 8.18:1 on white -- passes AAA)
- $mds-text-muted: #6a737b (contrast 4.83:1 on white -- passes AA)


Scope

In scope:
- Contrast and use-of-colour fixes for the new comment highlight animation in public/comment/comment.js
- Contrast fix for the textarea placeholder colour in public/comment/comment.js

Out of scope:
- Accessibility improvements to other comment implementations (e.g. mod/assign/feedback/comments, mod/workshop/form/comments)
- Structural refactoring of the YUI2-based comment system


Value

These are Level A and AA WCAG 2.2 failures that affect every Moodle user who posts or reads comments across the platform. Resolving them is a prerequisite for WCAG conformance claims and directly affects users with low vision or colour-perception difficulties.


Acceptance criteria

1. Text and link content within a newly posted comment that has received the highlight background colour meets SC 1.4.3 Contrast (Minimum) AA (4.5:1) for normal-weight text.
2. The username link within a highlighted new comment has a non-colour visual indicator distinguishing it as a link (e.g. underline), satisfying SC 1.4.1.
3. The textarea placeholder text meets SC 1.4.3 AA (4.5:1) contrast against its background.
4. Where design system tokens are available for the chosen colours, they are used in preference to hardcoded hex values.
5. All fixes are applied to main, MOODLE_502_STABLE, and MOODLE_501_STABLE.

title: Activity chooser: Filter tabs don't reflow at 400% zoom (WCAG 1.4.10)
description:
h3. Problem statement

On the Activity chooser page, when the viewport is narrow (e.g. 320x256 pixels, equivalent to 400% zoom on a standard 1280x1024 display), the content fails to reflow. The category filter tabs and the activity list do not adapt to the narrow viewport, and the fixed search header and footer occupy most of the available space. This is a violation of WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 (Reflow): https://www.w3.org/WAI/WCAG22/Understanding/reflow.html

h3. Who is affected

Any user with permission to add an activity or resource (e.g. teacher, course creator, manager, admin) who opens the Activity chooser, including users who rely on browser zoom or small viewports for accessibility reasons.

h3. Current behaviour

At 320x256 / 400% zoom, the Activity chooser does not reflow correctly:

* The search header and category filter tabs remain fixed/sticky at the top, consuming most of the vertical viewport.
* The footer remains fixed at the bottom with its current padding, further reducing usable space.
* Category tabs and activities do not stack, making the content impossible to read or use without horizontal scrolling.

See the attached screenshot below (image-20260624-083427.png) showing the problem at 400% zoom:

!image-20260624-083427.png|width=1174,alt="image-20260624-083427.png"!

h3. Expected behaviour

* The search header and category filter tabs should no longer be sticky/fixed; they should scroll up and out of the viewport with the rest of the page content. Their vertical padding should be reduced to give more room to the content below.
* The footer should remain sticky, but with reduced vertical padding so it takes up less of the viewport and leaves more room for content.
* Activity categories should stack vertically, one underneath the other, instead of being shown as horizontal tabs.
* Activities within a category should stack in a single column (one per row) underneath their category, rather than in a grid.
* See the attached mockup image category_example.png for the target category layout. Note: in that mockup the activities themselves are shown as rows of two — this is incorrect and must be implemented as rows of one (single column) instead, per the point above.

h3. Value

Fixes a WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 (Reflow) accessibility failure, allowing users who rely on browser zoom or small/narrow viewports to read and use the Activity chooser without loss of content or functionality and without horizontal scrolling.

h3. Scope

In scope:

* Activity chooser reflow at 320x256 viewport / 400% zoom equivalent.
* Making the search header and category tabs non-sticky, with reduced padding.
* Reducing footer padding while keeping it sticky.
* Stacking category tabs vertically.
* Stacking activities in a single column under their category.

Out of scope:

* Any other page or component reflow not related to the Activity chooser.
* Changes to activity chooser search/filter logic or functionality beyond layout/reflow.

h3. Acceptance criteria

* At a 320x256 viewport (or 400% zoom on a 1280x1024 display), the search header and category tabs scroll out of view with the page instead of remaining fixed, with reduced vertical padding.
* At the same viewport, the footer remains sticky but with reduced vertical padding.
* Category tabs are displayed stacked vertically, one under the other.
* Activities are displayed stacked in a single column (one per row) under their category.
* No horizontal scrolling or content clipping occurs at this viewport.
* Keyboard focus order remains logical after the layout changes to stacked categories/activities.
* Normal desktop-width behaviour (e.g. 1280x1024, no zoom) is unchanged.

h3. Notes

* This is an accessibility bug (WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.10 - Reflow).
* Original GrackleDocs finding: when zoomed to 400%, the page content is impossible to read as the fixed search header and footer occupy most of the viewport.
* Reference mockup for the category layout is attached as category_example.png. The activity layout in that mockup (rows of two) is not correct and must be implemented as rows of one instead.
* This bug requires patches on multiple supported Moodle versions (main, and the two most recent stable branches) in addition to main.
* See the Testing Instructions field on this issue for detailed step-by-step verification steps.

title: Allow column::add_fields() to accept array of field strings
description:
*Note:* *This ticket was created by an AI agent (GitHub Copilot)*

h2. Proposal: Union Type for column::add_fields()

h3. Current State

The {{add_fields()}} method in {{public/reportbuilder/classes/local/report/column.php}} accepts only a comma-separated string of fields. Internally it uses {{preg_split()}} to split the string back into individual fields. Some call sites have multiple fields to add, requiring them to use {{implode()}} before calling the method:

{code:php}->add_fields(implode(", ", [
    "{$tablealias}.id",
    "{$tablealias}.name",
    // ...
])){code}

This creates a redundant {{implode()}} then {{preg_split()}} round-trip.

h3. Proposal

Allow {{add_fields()}} to accept either a string *or* an array of field strings ({{string|array}}), enabling callers to pass arrays directly:

{code:php}->add_fields([
    "{$tablealias}.id",
    "{$tablealias}.name",
    // ...
]){code}

Each array element uses the same field syntax as the string format — {{table.field}}, {{table.field alias}}, or {{table.field AS alias}}.

h3. Affected Call Sites

Two instances in the codebase currently use the {{implode()}} pattern:

* {{public/reportbuilder/classes/local/systemreports/reports_list.php}} (line 129)
* {{public/webservice/classes/reportbuilder/local/systemreports/tokens.php}} (line 140)

h3. Benefits

* Cleaner, more readable call-site code
* Eliminates redundant string joining/parsing
* More intuitive API for callers with multiple fields
* Fully backward compatible — existing string calls are unaffected

title: Hardcoded dependencies on AI plugins breaks the site if they are uninstalled
description:
Summary:
Prevent optional AI placement plugins from breaking core course forms when they are uninstalled.

Problem statement:
Core course-management code directly calls utility classes from the optional aiplacement_courseassist and aiplacement_editor plugins. If either plugin is uninstalled, the corresponding class is unavailable and opening the affected course or activity form can fail with a missing-class error.

Affected direct dependencies:

* public/course/edit_form.php: aiplacement_courseassist\utils::is_course_assist_available()
* public/course/edit_form.php: aiplacement_editor\utils::is_html_editor_placement_available()
* public/course/modlib.php: aiplacement_courseassist\utils::get_actions_available($PAGE->context, false)
* public/course/modlib.php: aiplacement_editor\utils::get_actions_available($PAGE->context, false)
* public/course/moodleform_mod.php: aiplacement_courseassist\utils::is_course_assist_available()
* public/course/moodleform_mod.php: aiplacement_courseassist\utils::get_actions_available($this->get_context(), false)
* public/course/moodleform_mod.php: aiplacement_editor\utils::is_html_editor_placement_available()
* public/course/moodleform_mod.php: aiplacement_editor\utils::get_actions_available($this->get_context(), false)

Current behaviour:
On a site where either optional AI placement plugin has been uninstalled, a user can encounter a fatal error when opening affected course or activity editing workflows. The failure was introduced as part of the AI access-controls work in MDL-85738.

Expected behaviour:
Core course and activity workflows must continue to load when either optional AI placement plugin is not installed. AI controls and actions must continue to be shown only when their relevant placement is installed and available.

Architectural requirement:
aiplacement components are plugins and therefore optional. In line with Moodle's component-communication policy, core course code must not directly reference, load, or call a named placement plugin class, including behind a placement-specific class_exists() or equivalent guard.

The core AI subsystem provides the component-neutral integration point. Course code calls its manager API, which discovers installed and enabled AI placement plugins and obtains their context-specific availability and actions through the common core AI placement API. This discovery mechanism is an internal concern of the core AI subsystem; it does not require each placement plugin to implement a lib.php callback. Each placement owns its placement-specific availability, capability, and action behaviour. This keeps core course code independent of any particular placement and lets an optional placement be removed without changing core code.

Value:
Administrators can choose which optional AI placements to install without risking a site-breaking error in core course-management workflows.

Scope:

* Replace the direct dependencies listed above with the component-neutral core AI manager API.
* Preserve existing AI behaviour when the corresponding placement plugin is installed.
* Support main, Moodle 5.2.1, and Moodle 5.1.6.

Out of scope:

* Changing AI access-control rules or placement behaviour when all relevant plugins are installed.
* Requiring either optional placement plugin to remain installed.
* Adding a dependency from core course code to a specific placement plugin.

Acceptance criteria:

* Uninstalling aiplacement_courseassist does not cause an error when opening or editing a course or activity.
* Uninstalling aiplacement_editor does not cause an error when opening or editing a course or activity.
* Course code has no placement-specific direct class or utility calls; it uses the component-neutral core AI manager API.
* Core AI placement discovery excludes uninstalled and disabled placements.
* When a placement is installed and available, its existing course or editor AI controls and actions remain available according to current capability and availability checks.
* Automated regression coverage covers both installed and uninstalled placement cases.

Notes:

* This is a regression from MDL-85738 in the Moodle 5.1 series.
* This implementation must follow the Moodle component-communication policy.

title: Feedback: Replace text navigation in show responses view with icon pagination and sticky footer
description:
With the introduction of the core course linear navigation feature, which uses a text-based sticky footer ("Previous" / "Next") to cycle through course activities, the current layout of the mod_feedback response view introduces user experience friction:

!image-20260701-125253.png|width=600,alt="image-20260701-125253.png"!

To resolve this ambiguity, we will refactor the report navigation UX by replacing text links with compact, icon-only pagination buttons, as in the forum activity. We will add a sticky footer with a "Go to all responses" link, also like the forum. Using distinct chevrons clearly isolates the interaction to "navigating records within this report" rather than "moving to the next course activity":

!image-20260701-125348.png|width=600,alt="image-20260701-125348.png"!



h3. 🎯 Required actions

* Extract the text-based "◄ Prev", "Back", and "Next ►" action links from the feedback show responses view layout.
* Implement sticky footer: Call the {{set_supplementary_content()}} method to display the “Go to all responses” link.
* Replace textual pagination with standard core chevron icon components, with localised screen-reader text (aria-label), to ensure strict visual differentiation from primary course navigation text buttons.
* Update the relevant output renderers and mustache templates (within mod_feedback) to leverage core UI components and utility classes instead of inline or legacy structural styling.

h3. (/) Acceptance criteria

* The legacy text navigation links ("◄ Prev", "Back", "Next ►") are completely removed from the view.
* A sticky footer is implemented and anchors correctly at the bottom of the viewport.
* The page contains functional, rounded chevron/arrow buttons for "Previous" and "Next" records where applicable, eliminating text-based pagination controls.
* Accessibility compliance is maintained by applying localised aria-label attributes to the new icon controls (e.g., "Previous response", "Next response") so screen readers can clearly disambiguate them from course activity navigation.
* A "Go to all responses" link is centred within the sticky footer area and correctly redirects back to the response overview table.

title: Navigation footer: Hide sticky footer on portfolio pages

title: Implement REST API token entity and repository layer
description:
Implement the entity and repository for Non-OAuth2 REST API tokens under the {{core\api}} namespace.

It introduces the core domain model and persistence layer used to manage manually created REST API tokens. These tokens provide authenticated access to Moodle REST APIs without requiring an OAuth2 authorisation flow.

h4. Scope

* Implement {{\core\api\api_token_entity}}
** Domain model representing a REST API token.
* Implement {{\core\api\api_token_repository}}
** Repository responsible for persisting and retrieving REST API tokens.
* Unit test coverage.

title: Implement OAuth2 Server Scope repository layer including dynamic scope discovery engine
description:
Implement the Scope repository layer, including the infrastructure for dynamically discovering and registering API scopes within Moodle using a code-first approach.

Introduce a common scope abstraction and metadata attributes, enabling scopes to be declared as PHP classes rather than manually registered. The discovery mechanism should identify all concrete scope implementations across Moodle components, validate their declarations, and build an in-memory registry that can be consumed by the OAuth2 server and other authentication or authorisation services.

h4. In Scope

* Implement the Scope repository (ScopeRepositoryInterface)
* Introduce the base {{abstract_scope}} class that all API scopes need to extend.
* Implement PHP attributes for declaring scope metadata (name and description).
* Implement automatic discovery of scope classes across Moodle components.
* Build an in-memory registry of discovered scopes keyed by their qualified scope name.
* Unit test coverage.

title: core/string: Separate string-fetching utilities from the React String component
description:
Currently, {{public/lib/js/esm/src/String.tsx}} mixes two concerns in a single file:

# Plain TypeScript utilities for fetching, batching, and caching language strings ({{getRequestedStrings}}, {{getStrings}}, {{cacheStrings}}, {{getString}}, {{resetStringCache}}, and the {{StringParams}}/{{StringRequest}}/{{CacheStringEntry}} types).
# A React component ({{<String>}}) that wraps {{getString}} with {{Suspense}}/{{use()}} for JSX consumption.

This means any code that only needs the string-fetching logic (e.g. non-React modules, or unit tests) is forced to pull in a {{.tsx}} file with a React dependency.

This change extracts the pure-TypeScript logic into a new module, {{public/lib/js/esm/src/stringUtils.ts}}, with no functional changes. {{String.tsx}} now imports from {{stringUtils.ts}} and keeps only the React component ({{StringInner}}/{{<String>}}).

Since this API was only introduced in {{main}} and has not shipped in any release, it is not subject to backwards-compatibility requirements. All known callers have been updated to import directly from {{@moodle/lms/core/stringUtils}} instead of going through {{@moodle/lms/core/String}}:

* {{public/lib/js/esm/src/deprecated.ts}}
* {{public/lib/js/esm/tests/String.test.tsx}}
* {{.jest/globalSetup.ts}}
* {{public/lib/amd/src/str.js}} (the AMD {{core/str}} backward-compatibility shim, which loads the ESM module via {{core/esm!@moodle/lms/core/stringUtils}})

{{@moodle/lms/core/String}} no longer re-exports the string-fetching utilities — it exports only the {{<String>}} component and {{StringProps}}.

title: Implement OAuth 2 Server client manager class
description:
To support an internal OAuth2 authorisation server within Moodle, we need a centralised management class to handle CRUD operations for OAuth2 clients, their associated secrets, and redirect URIs.

Scope:

* The class should implement methods that allow
** Fetching clients
*** by ID
*** by client identifier
** Updating a client (restricted to modifying administrative metadata: name, description)
** Revoking a client
** Reactivating a revoked client
** Permanent deletion of a client
** Generation of client secrets (including a logic to enforce a maximum active secret limit per user to 2)
** Fetching client secrets
** Revoking client secrets
** Fetching redirect URIs
** Creation of redirect URIs
** Removal of redirect URIs
** Validation of redirect URIs
* Unit test coverage

h2. Clarifications

* *Secret limit scope*: the maximum of 2 active secrets is enforced *per client*, not per user (a user may own multiple clients, each with its own limit of 2 active secrets).
* *Client revocation cascade*: revoking a client immediately revokes all of that client's active tokens and secrets (integrates with the revocation logic in MDL-88473), fully cutting off access rather than just blocking new token issuance.
* *Reactivation semantics*: reactivating a revoked client only restores the client record itself. Previously-revoked secrets and tokens remain revoked; the client must generate new secrets and go through authorization again to obtain new tokens.
* *Deletion precondition*: permanent deletion is only allowed once a client is already in a revoked state. This acts as a safety guard against accidentally destroying a live integration.
* *Redirect URI validation*: URIs must match exactly (no prefix/wildcard matching) and must use HTTPS, except for {{localhost}}/loopback addresses (to support native app development). No cap on the number of redirect URIs per client.
* *Class design*: all methods must be instance methods (not static), and the class is expected to be loaded via dependency injection (Moodle's {{\core\di}} container), not instantiated directly or accessed via static/singleton patterns.

h2. Acceptance criteria

# All CRUD/lifecycle methods listed above are implemented with the rules described in Clarifications.
# Secret generation enforces the per-client limit of 2 active secrets.
# Revoking a client cascades to revoke its active tokens and secrets.
# Reactivating a client does not restore previously-revoked secrets/tokens.
# Permanent deletion is rejected unless the client is already revoked.
# Redirect URI validation rejects non-exact matches and non-HTTPS URIs (except localhost/loopback).
# The class exposes only instance methods and is resolvable via dependency injection.
# PHPUnit test coverage for all of the above, including edge cases (secret limit exceeded, delete-before-revoke rejection, invalid redirect URI schemes, reactivation not restoring secrets).

----

_Fleshed out via a grill-me session during the more-detail-needed/hqteam_tt grooming pass._

title: Create wireframes for OAuth2 client management
description:
Design the administrator-facing interface for managing registered OAuth2 clients.

This issue covers the user experience for listing, creating, viewing, editing, rotating credentials for, and deleting OAuth2 clients. It does not cover Personal Access Tokens, the OAuth login page, or the OAuth consent screen.

h2. Audience and access

The initial interface is for site administrators. The design should not prevent access being controlled by capabilities in a future iteration.

h2. Client model

Each client represents one integration or use case. For example, the Moodle mobile app and a server-to-server web-service integration should be represented by separate clients.

A client has an immutable type and primary OAuth2 flow. Administrators must create a new client rather than changing either value after creation.

h2. Client creation

The create flow should guide an administrator through:

# Choosing a client type:
#* Public
#* Confidential
# Choosing a permitted primary OAuth2 flow:
#* Public clients: Authorization Code, without a client secret.
#* Confidential clients: Authorization Code, with a client secret.
#* Confidential clients: Client Credentials, with a client secret.
#* Confidential clients: Resource Owner Password Credentials, with a client secret.

# Completing the relevant client configuration.

The selected client type and flow must be clearly explained during creation, including that they cannot be changed later.

h2. Client configuration

The wireframes should cover creating and editing a client, including:

* Name
* Description
* Icon
* Primary OAuth2 flow
* Client type
* Flow-specific settings
* Valid callback URIs where applicable:
** At least one callback URI is required for redirect-based flows.
** Only HTTPS, {{localhost}}, and {{127.0.0.1}} are permitted.

The design should show only configuration relevant to the selected client type and flow. For example, Client Credentials and Resource Owner Password Credentials clients do not require callback URI configuration.

*Permitted scopes*

Administrators configure the published OAuth scopes that a client is permitted to request.

Known Moodle integrations may begin with a recommended set of permitted scopes, which an administrator can restrict. Administrator-created clients begin with no permitted scopes selected and require explicit selection.

A client may request only a subset of its permitted scopes. The design must show the effect of removing a permitted scope, including that the updated policy applies to future authorisation and refresh activity. Exact token invalidation behaviour is to be confirmed during implementation design.

h2. Client list and details

Design:

* A list of registered clients with relevant identifying and security information, including at least name, client type, primary flow, status, and appropriate access metadata.
* A separate client detail page.
* Actions to edit a client, manage its secrets, and delete the client.
* Clear presentation of immutable fields, particularly client type and primary flow.

h2. Secrets and deletion

Confidential clients have client secrets.

The design must cover:

* Automatically generating a secret.
* Showing a newly generated secret one time only.
* Allowing up to two active secrets to support credential rotation.
* Revoking a secret permanently.
* Relevant metadata for each secret or token where available, including last access time and IP address.

Deleting a client permanently invalidates its active secrets and issued tokens. The design must include a clear confirmation flow for this irreversible action.

h2. Deliverables

Produce low- to medium-fidelity wireframes and supporting notes covering:

* Empty, populated, validation, error, confirmation, and irreversible-action states.
* The primary create, edit, secret rotation/revocation, and delete journeys.
* Any assumptions or unresolved design decisions.
* Accessibility and responsive considerations where they affect the interaction.

h2. Acceptance criteria

* Wireframes show permitted-scope selection in accordance with the OAuth2 administration design.
* The design implements the client type and flow model described above.
* Client type and primary OAuth2 flow are selectable only during creation and are read-only afterwards.
* PKCE is optional for Authorization Code clients and shown only where relevant.
* Public clients do not use client secrets; confidential clients do.
* Flow-specific configuration is shown only where relevant.
* Secret creation, one-time display, rotation, revocation, and client deletion states are clearly represented.
* The design is reviewed and agreed before implementation begins.

title: Create wireframes for Personal Access Token management
description:
Design the user-facing interface for creating and managing Personal Access Tokens (PATs).

This issue covers the self-service PAT interface in user preferences. It does not cover OAuth2 client management, the OAuth login page, or the OAuth consent screen.

h2. Audience and access

Access to PAT management is controlled by a capability.

Users can view and manage only their own PATs.

h2. PAT model

A user may have multiple active tokens.

Each token:

* Has a name and description.
* Has one or more selected scopes.
* Has a mandatory expiry date, no more than one year from its creation date.
* Is immutable after creation. Changing its name, description, expiry date, or scopes requires creating a new token.
* Becomes unusable automatically when it expires, but remains visible as an expired token until the user deletes it.

h2. Location and overview

The PAT interface should be available from user preferences.

Design a single management page that shows all relevant token information and actions without requiring a separate token-details page.

For each token, show at least:

* Name
* Description
* Scopes, with plain-language descriptions
* Created date
* Expiry date
* Last used time where available
* Status: active or expired

The page should provide an action to create a new token and appropriate empty states when the user has no tokens.

h2. Token creation

The create-token flow should allow the user to provide:

* Name
* Description
* Expiry date, validated to be in the future and no more than one year ahead
* One or more scopes

Scope selection should include a short plain-language description of the access granted by each scope. No additional warning is required for broad or sensitive scopes in the first version.

After creating a token:

* Display the token value once only.
* Provide a copy action.
* Clearly explain that the token value cannot be viewed again after leaving or acknowledging this screen.
* Do not reveal the token value in the management list after this point.

h2. Token deletion

Deleting an active token immediately revokes it and removes it from the active-token list.

Expired tokens remain visible until deleted.

The design must include clear confirmation flows for deleting active and expired tokens, making the consequences of deleting an active token explicit.

h2. Deliverables

Produce low- to medium-fidelity wireframes and supporting notes covering:

* The empty and populated token-management page.
* Creating a token, including scope selection and expiry-date validation.
* The one-time token display and copy experience.
* Active and expired token states.
* Deletion confirmation for active and expired tokens.
* Validation, error, and confirmation states.
* Any assumptions or unresolved design decisions.
* Accessibility and responsive considerations where they affect the interaction.

h2. Acceptance criteria

* Wireframes define a self-service PAT management experience in user preferences.
* Access is capability-controlled and users can manage only their own tokens.
* Users can create multiple tokens, each with one or more scopes and a mandatory expiry date of no more than one year.
* Token values are displayed and copyable once only after creation.
* Token settings cannot be changed after creation.
* The main page shows all relevant token metadata, including status, expiry, and available access information.
* Expired tokens remain visible until deleted.
* Deleting an active token revokes it immediately.
* The design is reviewed and agreed before implementation begins.

title: Tidy rendererables, renderers, and templates for login page
description:
Whilst working on [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88472|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88472|smart-link] I’ve found a number of minor issues with the login page, renderable, and template.

These issues include:

* when we dropped the boot bootstrap base theme we did not move the login page template from boost to core. Therefore we have two templates, but can only ever use _or test_ the boost variant. The one in core is entirely inaccessible to us, and therefore is a risk
* The {{$hasinstructions}} and {{$instructions}} template/php vars are no longer available
* The renderable is comprised of public properties which are calculated during construct, and never modified. These should be calculated during the export, and not public
* Whilst most values for the renderable are generated _within_ the renderable, a handful are generated _outside_ of it in the renderer, leading to duplication of this calculation logic.

I’m proposing:

# create a new {{loginform}} renderable, whose name matches the existing template - this allows for better backwards/forwards compatibility for plugins who are modifying the login form as they can continue to do so for <=5.2 and have a different way for 5.3+
# move the boost theme to core and remove the core variant
# drop unused parts of the template
# consolidate all of the template vars
# make all of the relevant class properties to be calculated during the export_for_template instead of the constructor and outside of the renderable

Note: This work is a precursor to [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88472|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88472|smart-link].

title: Drawer toggle/close icons (sidebar_left/sidebar_right) misaligned after SVG browser compatibility fix
description:
*Steps to reproduce:*

# Open dashboard/course page.
# Locate the left/right drawer toggle buttons (open course index / open blocks drawer), and the drawer close button once a drawer is open.

*Expected result:*

The sidebar arrow icons ({{e/sidebar_left}} and {{e/sidebar_right}}) are centered inside their buttons.

*Actual result:*

The icons appear slightly shifted to the left.

*Root cause:*

# MDL-88409 updated these icons to use a square {{viewBox="0 0 16 16"}}. However, the space used to display the icons ({{.icon-size-3 .icon}} in {{icons.scss}}) is *20×16*, not square.
# The *"*[*NOBUG: Fixed SVG browser compatibility*|https://github.com/moodle/moodle/commit/30926218ef33aa91363457616b475ba9a04f5177]*"* change added {{preserveAspectRatio="xMinYMid meet"}} to these SVGs to fix a browser compatibility issue. 
The {{xMin}} value aligns the SVG content to the left instead of the center. Because the SVG is *16×16* but the icon container is *20×16*, the icons end up looking slightly left of center.
[https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Reference/Attribute/preserveAspectRatio|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Reference/Attribute/preserveAspectRatio|smart-link]

title: Create backend OAuth 2 Server implementation
description:

title: File picker content area (.fp-content) uses a fixed height: 452px that overflows the dialogue on short (laptop) viewports
description:
h3. Impact

The file picker dialog can overflow the viewport on short laptop-sized screens.  
Users may see the picker content cut off or spilling outside the dialog.

h3. Expected behaviour

The picker content should size to its content.  
The dialog should stay within the viewport, even when the folder is empty.

!image-20260726-023127.png|width=671,alt="image-20260726-023127.png"!



h3. Actual behaviour

The {{.fp-content}} area is forced to a fixed height of 452px, even in the empty state.  
This makes the content area extend past the dialog and viewport boundary.  
Part of the picker is cut off or spills out.

!image-20260726-023054.png|width=671,alt="image-20260726-023054.png"!



h3. Steps to reproduce

* Use a browser window with a short viewport height, for example a laptop screen or a window resized to about 650px usable height.
* Go to any file field, for example:
** Course administration → Edit settings → Course image
** Any Files and uploads field
* Open the file picker.
* Select Server files, or any repository.
* Navigate into an empty folder with “No files available”.

h3. Environment

* Short viewport heights, such as laptop screens.
* Browser windows resized to a short usable height.
* File picker dialogs using {{responsiveWidth: 768}}.

h3. Workarounds

No workaround was provided.

h3. Other information

{{theme/boost/scss/moodle/filemanager.scss}} (in 5.1+: {{public/theme/boost/scss/moodle/filemanager.scss}}):

{code:css}.file-picker .fp-content {
    border-top: 0;
    background: $filemanager-picker-bg;
    clear: none;
    overflow: auto;
    height: 452px;   // ← fixed height, applied even to the empty state
}{code}

Combined with the fixed, width-only-responsive dialogue in {{repository/filepicker.js}} (≈ lines 1462–1486):

{code:javascript}var width = 873;                 // fixed width
...
this.mainui = new M.core.dialogue({
    ...
    width: width + 'px',
    responsiveWidth: 768,        // responsive on width only
    height: '558px',             // fixed height, no vertical responsiveness
    ...
});{code}

There is no vertical responsiveness, so on short viewports the fixed 452px content cannot shrink and overflows.

core/react_autoinit: async component mounts aren't tracked as pending JS
description:
{{core/react_autoinit}} scans the DOM for {{data-react-component}} elements and mounts each one asynchronously: it dynamically imports the component module, then renders it into the placeholder element.  This is the shared mounting mechanism used by every React component mounted via the {{{{#react}}}} mustache helper, not specific to any one component.

The mount function never calls {{Pending.complete()}},  so Behat's wait-for-pending-JS mechanism has no way to know a mount is in progress.

This surfaced while working on [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87830|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87830|smart-link] , where it caused intermittent "element not found" / "not interactable" Behat failures immediately after navigating to a page with a React-mounted secondary nav

title: Assignment grades remain editable in workflow states unavailable to the grader
description:
h2. Background

The {{assign::grading_disabled}} and {{assign::update_grade}} methods read {{workflowstate}} from the *assign_grades* record, however it’s stored in {{assign_user_flags}}. The checks therefore do nothing, allowing graders to edit grades in workflow states they cannot manage. A similar issue was identified in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-70441).|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-70441).|smart-link] .

This issue also covers multiple marking: once the overall workflow state is “Ready for release” or “Released”, individual marker marks must not be modified, including by users with permission to manage or release the overall workflow state.

h2. Replication steps

# Create a grader role with *mod/assign:grade*, but _without_ *mod/assign:reviewgrades*, mod/*assign:releasegrades*, or *mod/assign:managegrades*
# Create an assignment with marking workflow enabled
# Have a student submit
# As a teacher or administrator, give the submission a grade and set its workflow state to “Released”
# Log in as the grader and open the student’s grading page
# Change the grade and save it

*Expected*: The grade is read only because “Released” is not a workflow state available to this grader.
*Actual*: The grade remains editable and the released grade can be changed.

For multiple marking, the expected result is individual marker marks must also be read only once the overall state is “Ready for release” or “Released”, including for users who can manage or release that state.

title: Learning outcomes: New page to view course learning outcomes and associated activities
description:
Now that we have the ability to create both scaled and scaleless learning outcomes, we need a way to present this information to users in a clear and intuitive way.

*Scope*

# A new “Learning outcomes” item in the course “More” menu, which navigates to a new page within the course.
# The Page should display all learning outcomes enabled for the current course. We do not need to differentiate whether they include a scale or not, the scales are handled separately in the gradebook.
# Each outcome should be a collapsible section, which lists the activities assigned to that learning outcome.
# This page should look consistent with the course UI uplift version of the course homepage (rather than the old one), if it is possible. This means each learning outcome should behave like a section on the course homepage, and each activity within it should  appear with same styling/iconography as activities under sections on the homepage. We do not need to include all of the dates, completion criteria etc shown on the homepage.
# Currently we have the [rapid prototype|https://whiterabbit.gallery/learning-outcomes-course-view/v1/] of this page, this issue will be updated if/when we have a Figma prototype or some other design. *EDIT:* Here is the [Figma prototype|https://www.figma.com/design/0g1LJWk3uyy2Le4918xFWl/MDL-89334---Learning-Outcomes-Uplift?node-id=5-167&p=f&t=DOubj6kqppcrv1si-0].

*Out of scope*

# Improved teacher management of the learning outcomes (coming later).
# Functionality to display any learning outcomes information on the course homepage (we may add a block similar to that on the rapid prototype in the future).

This is the final piece of functionality required for the project MVP, as it allows students and teachers to view both the full list of learning outcomes for a course, as well as the activities assigned to those outcomes.

title: Create developer documentation for OAuth2 Server
description:
Document the OAuth2 Server API in the developer docs.

h4. Architecture and Integration

* *Library Version*: Specify the exact {{league/oauth2-server}} version used and how it is loaded.
* *Repository/Service Mappings*: Document how Moodle's user database and session layer interface with standard [PHP League Repositories|https://oauth2.thephpleague.com/] (AccessTokenRepository, ClientRepository, ScopeRepository, UserRepository, etc).
* *Encryption Keys*: Detail where private and public cryptographic keys are stored securely on the server path and how they are generated.

h4. Endpoints and Routing

* *Route Mapping*: List custom Moodle web service endpoints or router end-points
* *Supported Grants*: Document which grant types are active

h4. Administration and Security

* *Client Management*: Document how third-party client credentials (Client ID, Secret, Redirect URIs) are provisioned, stored, and managed in Moodle tables.
* *Scopes*: How does the dynamic scope discivery mechanism works and how to define custom Moodle scopes including how user consent or capability checks are evaluated.
* *Token Lifetimes*: Record configuration settings for access token and refresh token expiration intervals.

title: Allow obtaining multiple markers feedback via WebServices
description:
In [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86007|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86007|smart-link] , the multiple markers feature was modified to let each marker add different feedback via plugins (e.g. each marker has its own feedback comments, or feedback files). And the student can see the feedback of each marker, along with the overall (general) feedback.

Since this change affects students, we would like to support the students part in the Moodle app, so students can also see the feedback for each marker in there. However, the WebServices weren’t modified as part of this issue, so right now there’s no way to obtain that information via WebService.

The WebService that currently returns the feedback is {{mod_assign_get_submission_status}}. In an assign with multiple markers, it’s only returning the overall/generic feedback, but not the feedback for each marker. We should probably modify the WebService to also return the feedback for each marker (when the user calling the WebService is allowed to see this information).

title: Notify users when a personal access token is about to expire
description:
Notify a user when one of their personal access tokens is nearing its expiry date, so they can create a replacement before it stops working. This covers the notification only — creation, display, and deletion of tokens is handled in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89185|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89185|smart-link].

Notification channels:

* Email, sent to the user's account email address.
* A Moodle notification, delivered through the standard notification system (so it also respects the user's notification preferences, e.g. email digest settings, and appears in the notification bell/list).

Notification content should include the token's name, its expiry date, and a link to the personal access token management page so the user can act on it directly.

Open questions to resolve before/during design:

* How far ahead of expiry should the first (and any repeat) reminder be sent — e.g. 7 days, with a possible second reminder at 1 day?
* Should this be a one-time reminder or repeat until the token is renewed/deleted or actually expires?
* Should there be a separate notification when the token actually expires, distinct from the "about to expire" warning?
* Should users be able to opt out of this notification type, consistent with Moodle's general notification preference model?

*Acceptance criteria:*

* Users receive an email and a Moodle notification before a personal access token expires.
* The notification identifies the specific token and links to the management page.
* Notification timing and repeat behaviour are defined and documented.
* Notification preferences follow Moodle's standard notification framework where applicable.

title: TinyMCE Premium: get_api_key always returns usecloud=true regardless of the self-hosted plugin source setting
description:
h4. Problem statement

{{tiny_premium\external\get_api_key::execute()}} determines whether Tiny Premium plugins should be loaded from Tiny Cloud or from the self-hosted package based on the {{tiny_premium/plugin_source}} admin setting.

The comparison used to make this decision is incorrect, causing self-hosted sites to always fall back to loading premium plugins from Tiny Cloud regardless of the configured plugin source.

h4. Current behaviour

* {{get_api_key.php}} compares {{get_config('tiny_premium', 'plugin_source')}} with {{manager::PACKAGE_SELF_HOSTED}} using a strict {{!==}} comparison.
* {{get_config()}} returns configuration values as strings, while {{manager::PACKAGE_SELF_HOSTED}} is an integer.
* As a result, the strict comparison always evaluates to {{true}}, so {{usecloud}} is always set to {{true}}.
* Therefore, setting *Plugin source* to *Self-hosted* has no effect. Premium plugins are still loaded from Tiny Cloud, including the associated CDN requests.

h4. Steps to reproduce

# Configure {{tiny_premium/plugin_source}} to *Self-hosted*, with a valid self-hosted path configured for the base TinyMCE package.
# Enable a premium plugin, for example Markdown, and load the editor.
# Open the browser network tab and observe that the premium plugin script is requested from {{cdn.tiny.cloud}} instead of the configured self-hosted path.

h4. Expected behaviour

When {{plugin_source}} is set to *Self-hosted*, {{usecloud}} should evaluate to {{false}}, and the premium plugins should be loaded from the local self-hosted files instead of Tiny Cloud.

h4. Root cause

This is a type mismatch: a string returned by {{get_config()}} is being compared to an integer constant using {{!==}}.

h4. Fix

Cast the configuration value to an integer before performing the comparison:

{code:javascript}'usecloud' => (int) get_config('tiny_premium', 'plugin_source') !== manager::PACKAGE_SELF_HOSTED,{code}

The fix has already been applied on {{main}} as part of [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88547|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88547|smart-link].

This ticket is only to backport the same fix to the *5.1 and 5.2*, which include the self-hosted Tiny Premium support introduced by [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-85727|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-85727|smart-link]

title: MDL-88407 multiplicator/offset assignment grading fix does not freeze grades
description:
When [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88407|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-88407|smart-link] was applied, it unintentionally missed our [process to freeze affected grades|https://docs.moodle.org/dev/How_to_fix_gradebook_issues].

We need to freeze existing grades in line with that process, because there are ways for a re-grade to be triggered automatically, for example by adding a new grade item. Below is a video of that example, showing the grade change once a grade item is added.

*Video example:*

[^Regrade-2026-08-17 17-12-55.mkv]



Root cause (SS updated this for further review and development work): *Anyone reviewing should read this.*

The gradebook stores two numbers for each grade: {{rawgrade}} (the original mark from the activity, for example 50/100 from an assignment) and {{finalgrade}} (what appears in the gradebook after applying the grade item's multiplicator/offset and any penalty).

*Before MDL-88407*, the penalty code did things in the wrong order. When a penalty was deducted, it took the final grade (which already had the multiplicator applied), subtracted the penalty, and wrote the result back into {{rawgrade}}. The gradebook then applied the multiplicator _again_ to compute finalgrade. With multiplicator 1.1, a mark of 50 with a 10-point late penalty was stored as {{rawgrade = 45}} (that is 50×1.1 − 10, a value that already contains the multiplicator) and displayed as 49.5 (45×1.1, multiplicator applied twice). MDL-88407 fixed the formula, {{rawgrade}} now always keeps the original mark (50), the penalty is subtracted from the raw mark, and factors are applied once: finalgrade = (50 − 10) × 1.1 = 44.

*The regression*: the fix changed the formula but did nothing to address the already-stored corrupted rows and did not freeze the affected courses. Moodle's standard process for calculation-changing fixes ("gradebook freeze") requires that existing grades stay untouched until a teacher explicitly accepts the change. Without the freeze, the moment anything triggers a regrade (adding a grade item, changing course settings, etc.), the _new_ formula is applied to the _old corrupted_ {{rawgrade}}: (45 − 10) × 1.1 = 38.5. The student's visible grade changes silently from 49.5 to 38.5, and it's wrong in both worlds: neither the old value (49.5) nor the truly correct one (44).

title: OAuth2 clients are not enforcing the PKCE requirement
description:
*Description*

MDL-88468 currently allows an administrator to enable PKCE when creating a client. This setting is stored as {{ispkceenabled}} and exposed through {{client_entity::is_pkce_enabled()}}.

However, the authorization flow does not currently use this setting. The {{AuthCodeGrant}} configuration in MDL-88472 also calls:

{noformat}->method('disableRequireCodeChallengeForPublicClients'){noformat}

This disables the League OAuth2 Server library’s default requirement for public clients to provide a code challenge.

As a result, the UI, stored client configuration and authorization behaviour do not currently agree.

This issue should first decide whether Moodle wants to support configurable PKCE. Based on that decision, we should either:

# Keep the PKCE option and implement the corresponding authorization behaviour, including the expected behaviour for public and confidential clients; or
# Remove the PKCE option and its supporting fields from the client management implementation.

If PKCE remains supported, we should also decide:

* whether it is mandatory for public clients;
* whether it is optional or configurable for confidential clients;
* whether both {{plain}} and {{S256}} challenge methods are supported, or only {{S256}}.

*Acceptance criteria*

# The expected PKCE behaviour for public and confidential clients is documented in this issue.
# The client management UI only displays PKCE configuration that is supported by the authorization flow.
# Stored client configuration and authorization behaviour agree.
# If PKCE is required for a client, an authorization request without a valid {{code_challenge}} is rejected.
# When PKCE is used, the token request rejects a missing or invalid {{code_verifier}}.
# Automated tests cover the agreed behaviour for public and confidential clients.
# The behaviour of the following combinations is explicitly tested where applicable:
#* public client without PKCE;
#* public client with valid PKCE;
#* confidential client without PKCE;
#* confidential client with valid PKCE;
#* invalid challenge method;
#* missing or incorrect verifier.

title: React nav: active items in the "More" menu lost their tick and active styling
description:
In 5.2 an active item inside the "More" dropdown was shown with a checkmark and the theme's active treatment (dark text on grey, blue on hover/focus). Since the React migration (in MDL-87830) it gets Bootstrap's plain .dropdown-item.active look (blue background, white text) and no checkmark. In MDL-87830 a shared React nav engine was introduced, which is used in both the primary and secondary navigation.

|!custommenu-502.png|width=274,alt="custommenu-502.png"!|!3f240295-2be9-4cbb-a51e-382a6f2ac514.png|width=304,alt="3f240295-2be9-4cbb-a51e-382a6f2ac514.png"!|



*Cause*

Two changes in core/nav/Nav, neither of which the theme rules were updated for:

# Dropdown items render aria-current="page" (Nav.tsx, DropdownItems/DropdownSubmenu) rather than the legacy aria-current="true". Boost's checkmark rules key off [aria-current="true"] / [aria-selected="true"] — see theme/boost/scss/moodle/action-menu.scss and moremenu.scss — so they no longer match.
# Both React mount points deliberately omit the legacy "moremenu" class (primarymoremenu.mustache, secondarymoremenu.mustache), because those rules are written for the legacy <li>-wrapped markup. That also excludes the ".moremenu .dropdown-item.active" treatment (transparent background, body text colour, checkmark, blue on hover/focus-within).

For reference, in 5.2 the .active class on a dropdown item came from moremenu.js's moveIntoMoreDropdown(), which swapped nav-link -> dropdown-item on the moved link and set aria-current="true"; nested submenu children were rendered with aria-current="true" and no .active. React renders that end state directly instead.

*Steps to reproduce*

# Site administration > Appearance > Advanced theme settings, add:
{noformat}Courses|/course/
  -All courses|/course/index.php
  -Course search|/course/search.php{noformat}
# Narrow the browser until "Courses" collapses into the "More" menu.
# Go to /course/search.php, then open "More" > "Courses".

*Expected:* "Course search" (and the "Courses" parent) show a checkmark, as in 5.2.
*Actual:* no checkmark; the active item uses Bootstrap's blue/white active style.

*Suggested fix*

Keep aria-current="page" — it matches @moodlehq/design-system's NavPill and behat_navigation.php already accepts both "true" and "page" — and add active-item rules scoped to the React dropdown (.dropdownmoremenu > .dropdown-menu) mirroring the existing
.moremenu block, so both navigations regain the 5.2 appearance.



*Note:* This ticket also fixes the dark mode compatibility raised in [https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89686|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-89686|smart-link]. Since the darkmode fix is trivial and it’s testing instructions will be almost identical, its easier to fix and test here.

!Screenshot From 2026-09-03 10-03-18.png|width=864,alt="Screenshot From 2026-09-03 10-03-18.png"!

It displays correctly on 5.2:

!Screenshot From 2026-09-03 10-24-21.png|width=835,alt="Screenshot From 2026-09-03 10-24-21.png"!

h3. Why it happens (AI generated, please double check)

The row of dropdowns is a flex container with wrapping turned on ({{d-flex flex-wrap}}), and it has 582px of space inside its column.

* Without the Enable checkbox, the row needs 504px — it fits.
* The Enable checkbox adds 83px, so the row needs 587px — 5px too wide.

The calendar icon is the last item in the row, so it is the one that wraps.

h3. Notes

* This is not a small-screen problem. The form is capped at 784px wide, so making the browser window wider does not help — it still reproduces at 1920px.
* Only date-and-time fields with an Enable checkbox are affected (course end date, activity due dates, cutoff dates). Date fields without the checkbox are fine.
* 5px is a thin margin, so other languages may behave differently — the month dropdown is sized by the longest month name.

Same symptom as [MDL-62730|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-62730], which was fixed in 3.5.1 by adding {{align-items-center}}. This is a separate cause (wrapping, not vertical alignment).

Tested on main (5.3dev, build 20260818), Boost theme, clean checkout.

title: OAuth2 Client should be authorised for web service calls
description:
We’ve missed this in our initial implementaiton. We have all of the login flows, access tokens, etc… but they can’t actually do anything.

We need to allow authorised OAuth2 and PAT users to access v2 web services and all of the missing work to support this.

To do this we need:

* to update the API Authentication middleware to check for the OAuth2 and PAT bearer token in the header and complete a _cookie-less_ login if valid
** If not specified then silently move to the next auth mech;
** If not valid then exception thrown
* to validate the OAuth2 /  PAT scopes for the specific web service requested
* to set the scopes on the web services (MDL-88710)
* to ensure that we authenticate before validating headers, and params

In doing the work for this I’ve also discovered some issues with the PAT system:

* we should be passing around arrays of strings, not a space-separated string
* the token *must* be base64-encoded. It currently isn’t.

title: Third-party library versions in composer.json out of sync with thirdpartylibs.xml (slim/slim, aws/aws-sdk-php)
description:
h2. What is this issue?

Two third-party libraries have a different version pinned in the root {{composer.json}} than the version actually shipped in {{public/lib}} and recorded in {{public/lib/thirdpartylibs.xml}}.

||Package||thirdpartylibs.xml||composer.json / composer.lock||
|{{slim/slim}}|4.15.1|4.13.0|
|{{aws/aws-sdk-php}}|3.369.22|3.356.22|

The versions in {{thirdpartylibs.xml}} are the correct ones. They match the code on disk:

* {{public/lib/slim/slim/CHANGELOG.md}} - latest entry is 4.15.1
* {{public/lib/aws-sdk/src/Sdk.php:838}} - {{const VERSION = '3.369.22'}}

So it is {{composer.json}} (and the resulting {{composer.lock}}) that is stale.

h2. How did this happen?

[MDL-87950|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87950] added all unmodified third-party libraries to {{composer.json}}, pinned at the exact version shipped in Moodle. It landed on 2026-03-04.

Two library upgrades that landed afterwards updated {{thirdpartylibs.xml}} but not {{composer.json}}:

* [MDL-86456|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86456] - Upgrade Slim Framework to 4.15.1 (2026-03-12)
* [MDL-87598|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-87598] - Upgrade AWS SDK for PHP to 3.369.22 (2026-04-15)

This was spotted by Daniel Ziegenberg on [MDL-86456|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86456], who commented: _"You forgot to update the version of slim in composer.json."_

For reference, other upgrades from the same period did remember to do this: [MDL-86462|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86462] (Guzzle), [MDL-86460|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86460] (laravel/serializable-closure) and [MDL-86406|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-86406] (ADOdb) all include a matching {{composer.json}} bump.

h2. Proposed fix

# {{composer.json:60}} - change {{"slim/slim": "4.13.0"}} to {{"4.15.1"}}
# {{composer.json:81}} - change {{"aws/aws-sdk-php": "3.356.22"}} to {{"3.369.22"}}
# Regenerate {{composer.lock}} 

No change is needed in {{public/lib/thirdpartylibs.xml}} or in any library code.

title: Secrets are permanently revoked during client revocation
description:
Revoking an OAuth2 client currently permanently revokes all associated client secrets which is not a desirable behavior. When an administrator re-enables the client later, those secrets remain permanently revoked and unusable, forcing full re-generation and re-distribution of credentials to external services.

Client revocation should function as an administrative suspension: it must permanently invalidate all active tokens and authorization codes, but preserve secrets so integrations can be temporarily paused and resumed without breaking existing credential configurations.

*Steps to Reproduce*:

# Create an OAuth2 client and generate a client secret.
# Revoke the client.
# Re-enable the client in the administrative interface.
# It’s not possible to authenticate using the original client secret.

*Expected Behavior*:

* *Token Invalidation:* Revoking a client permanently revokes all active access tokens, refresh tokens, and authorization codes.
* *Secret Preservation:* Secrets retain their un-revoked status when the parent client is revoked, but are blocked at runtime while the client is inactive.
* *Secret Status UI:* The secrets management table displays a computed status such as {{Inactive}} with an explanatory notice while the parent client is revoked.
* *Re-enablement:* Re-enabling the client restores functionality to existing active secrets without reviving old tokens.

title: Notify users and admins when a personal access token or client secret is created
description:
Notify people when a credential is issued, so an unexpected one is noticed. Security counterpart to the expiry warning in MDL-89442.

Personal access token created: notify the owning user. This is what catches a compromised account.

Client secret created: notify administrators, since these are site level credentials.

Both go out by email and Moodle notification, following the channels proposed in MDL-89442. Content identifies the credential (name, expiry, link to the management page) and never includes the token or secret value.

Neither creation path fires an event today, so add the events first and have the notification subscribe to them. That gives administrators log entries for credential creation as well as the message.

*Open questions*

* Which administrators receive the client secret notice, all of them or a capability?
* Is the creator notified of their own action?
* Opt out, or always on as a security notice?

*Acceptance criteria*

* User notified when a personal access token is created on their account.
* Administrators notified when a client secret is created.
* Notifications link to the management page and never contain the credential value.
* Events fired for both paths and visible in the site logs.

title: Client Credentials primary flow should not be checked by default
description:
At the moment, when creating a new client both of the flows are enabled by default:

* Authorization code
* Client Credentials

We should change this and add warnings. Specifically though we should not have the *Client Credentials* flow enabled by default.

The reason for this change is that the Client Credentials grant requires no subsequent login step. The client id and secret will allow a client connecting with the client credentials grant *_admin_* access to Moodle.

We need to, at the very least, change the default value to *not* check *client credentials* and, ideally, to have a warning about how access will work.

I’m also yet to find a use-case for providing multiple auth flows (auth + client) in a single set of credentials. Looking at other similar consoles I haven’t found one which does this yet. 

Personally I would say we should _not_ allow multiple flow types in a single client.

title: Create personal access token: the "no scopes selected" error is not exposed to assistive technology (WCAG 3.3.1)
description:
Submitting the _Create a personal access token_ form with no scopes ticked produces the visible error "Select at least one scope for the token." That message is not associated with anything, nothing is marked invalid, and focus is not moved, so a screen reader user is given no indication that the submission failed.

This fails *SC 3.3.1 Error Identification, Level A*: the error is described in text, but the item that is in error is not identified.

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Go to _Preferences > Personal access tokens_ and select *Create token*.
# Enter a name and leave every scope checkbox unticked.
# Select *Create token*.

h2. Measured

The page reloads with the error rendered, and:

|| || ||
|Error element|{{#id_error_scopeslabel}}, class {{form-control-feedback invalid-feedback}}|
|{{role}} / {{aria-live}} on it|*none*|
|Elements with {{aria-invalid="true"}}|*none*|
|Elements with {{aria-describedby}} pointing at the error|*none*|
|{{is-invalid}} class on any control|*none*|
|{{document.activeElement}} after submit|{{BODY}}|

So the sequence for a screen reader user is: activate Create token, the page reloads, focus is on the body, and nothing is announced. The error text exists on screen but is not reachable through any relationship from a form control.

h2. The same form handles single-field errors correctly

This is the useful comparison, and it shows core {{moodleform}} is not at fault. Clearing the *Name* field and submitting gives:

|| ||Name error||Scopes error||
|{{aria-invalid}}|{{true}}|none|
|{{aria-describedby}}|{{id_error_name}}, resolves|none|
|{{is-invalid}} class|present|none|
|Focus after submit|moves to {{#id_name}}|stays on {{BODY}}|

mform does the right thing whenever the error belongs to a real form control.

h2. Cause

{{lib/classes/api/form/create_token.php}} reports the scopes error against a {{static}} element:

{code:php}protected const string SCOPE_LABEL = 'scopeslabel';

$mform->addElement(
    'static',
    self::SCOPE_LABEL,
    get_string('pat_scopes') . ' ' . $OUTPUT->pix_icon('req', ...),
    $OUTPUT->notification(get_string('pat_scopesinfo'), 'info', false),
);
...
public function validation($data, $files): array {
    ...
    $errors[self::SCOPE_LABEL] = get_string('apitokennoscopes', 'error');
}{code}

A {{static}} element is not a form control, so mform has nothing to set {{aria-invalid}} or {{aria-describedby}} on, and nothing for focus management to target. It renders the message and stops there.

There is no fallback either, because the 21 scope checkboxes are not grouped. Each is added as its own {{advcheckbox}} in its own form row, with a deliberate comment explaining why a group was avoided:

{code:php}// A checkbox per scope, each its own form row: a form group would lay them out inline,
// and a description too wide for the rest of the line drops beneath its own checkbox.{code}

That layout reasoning is sound, but it leaves the group-level error with no host element. The form also renders no {{fieldset}}, no {{legend}} and no headings at all, so there is nothing in the accessibility tree that represents "the scopes for this token" as a unit.

h2. Suggested fix

Give the scopes a real group and attach the error to it:

# Wrap the 21 checkboxes in a {{fieldset}} with a {{legend}} carrying the _Scopes_ label and its required marker. A {{fieldset}} does not force the inline layout the comment was avoiding, so this should not disturb the current presentation.
# Point {{aria-describedby}} on that {{fieldset}} at {{#id_error_scopeslabel}} when the error is present, and set {{aria-invalid="true"}} on it, mirroring what mform already does for single controls.
# Move focus to the group on a failed submit, as the form already does for {{#id_name}}.

An alternative is to attach the error to the first scope checkbox rather than to the static element, which would get {{aria-invalid}} and {{aria-describedby}} for free from mform. That is less accurate, because the error describes the set rather than that one control, so the {{fieldset}} is the better shape.

Worth adding a Behat assertion for the error state while in there, since the current {{personalaccesstokens.feature}} covers the happy path.

h2. Scope

Only the create form is affected. The rest of the feature measured clean under axe-core 4.10.2 with the tag set {{behat_accessibility}} uses, at a viewport confirmed at 1280x900:

* the empty state, the create form and the token reveal screen each report *0 violations*
* the reveal screen is well built: the warning carries {{role="alert"}}, the token field is {{readonly}} with a real {{<label for>}}, the copy button carries visible text beside its icon at a 96x38 target, and {{core/copy_to_clipboard}} announces success through {{core/toast}} ({{role="status"}}) and returns focus to the button
* the token table has a {{<caption>}} and proper {{<thead>}} headers, and its 29 padding rows are {{display: none}} so they are not exposed

Found during the Moodle 5.3 accessibility review.

title: LTI 1.3 content-item selection modal is too small for tools with substantial configuration UIs
description:
Clicking *Select content* on an External tool opens the Deep Linking (content-item) UI in a modal fixed at roughly 770 x 578px, regardless of viewport. Tools with a substantial configuration form cannot fit their UI, and the modal neither widens nor grows taller on large displays.

Two independent causes.

*1. Width capped at `modal-lg` (800px).*

{{public/mod/lti/amd/src/contentitem.js:70}} passes {{large: true}} to {{Modal.create()}}. {{Modal.setLarge()}} ({{public/lib/amd/src/modal.js:744}}) only ever adds {{modal-lg}}, and {{$modal-lg}} is {{800px}} ({{lib/bundles/bootstrap/scss/_variables.scss:1534}}).

*2. Height is derived from width, so it cannot grow.*

{{public/mod/lti/templates/contentitem.mustache:79-84}}:

{noformat}var containerWidth = $('div.contentitem-container').width();
$('#contentitem-page-iframe').width(containerWidth + 'px');

// Adjust iframe's height to 75% of the width.
var containerHeight = containerWidth * 0.75;
$('#contentitem-page-iframe').height(containerHeight + 'px');{noformat}

With width capped at ~770px, height is permanently ~578px. There are no {{.contentitem-container}} or {{.contentitem-page}} rules in {{public/mod/lti/styles.css}} — all sizing lives in this inline template JS.

This is a regression from the same commit: the code [MDL-49609|https://moodle.atlassian.net/browse/MDL-49609] replaced derived height from the dialogue container ({{dialogueContainer.height() - 55}}).

h2. Impact

Reported by Turnitin, who treat it as blocking rather than cosmetic: their Feedback Studio assignment-creation UI does not fit the modal, and they cite it as a primary reason institutions have not migrated from their legacy Moodle plugins to the LTI 1.3 integration.

This is time-bound. Turnitin have confirmed that future Feedback Studio development targets the LTI 1.3 workflow only, with no further improvements to the plugins, and their LTI 1.1 support ends 31 December 2026. Institutions on the legacy plugins therefore have a fixed deadline to move onto an integration that this defect makes impractical to use.
